definition_zh: 置信区间
definition_en: a range of values calculated from sample data that is expected to contain the true parameter at a stated confidence level over repeated sampling

senses.title: A range built around an estimate
senses.titleCN: 围绕估计值构造的范围
senses.definition: an interval computed from sample data so that it is likely to contain the unknown parameter
senses.definitionCN: 由样本数据算出、很可能包含未知参数的区间
senses.example: A confidence interval shows the range that repeated samples would usually bracket.
senses.exampleCN: 置信区间显示反复抽样通常会框住的数值范围。
senses.why: A single number hides its own uncertainty, so the interval gives the uncertainty a visible width.
senses.whyCN: 单个数字把自己的不确定性藏了起来，区间则给这份不确定性一个可见的宽度。

senses.title: The long-run coverage interpretation
senses.definition: the interpretation that, across many repeated samples, the stated proportion of such intervals will contain the true value
senses.definitionCN: 在大量重复抽样中，所述比例的区间会包含真值的解释
senses.example: A ninety-five per cent confidence interval does not mean a ninety-five per cent chance for this one interval.
senses.exampleCN: 百分之九十五的置信区间并不意味着这一个区间有百分之九十五的概率包含真值。
senses.why: The confidence belongs to the procedure that builds intervals, not to any single interval after it is built.
senses.whyCN: 信心属于构造区间的程序，而不属于建成之后的某一个区间。

senses.title: The confidence level
senses.definition: the stated proportion, usually ninety-five or ninety-nine per cent, attached to the procedure
senses.definitionCN: 附在程序上的所述比例，通常为百分之九十五或九十九
senses.example: Raising the confidence level widens the interval for the same data.
senses.exampleCN: 在数据相同的情况下，提高置信水平会使区间变宽。
senses.why: More confidence requires a wider net, and a wider net catches more but says less about where the value lies.
senses.whyCN: 更高的信心需要更宽的网，网更宽能兜住更多，却更难说清值在哪里。

senses.title: The margin around the point estimate
senses.definition: the distance from the estimate to each end of the interval, often built from a standard error and a multiplier
senses.definitionCN: 从估计值到区间两端的距离，常由标准误与倍数构成
senses.example: The confidence interval is the estimate plus and minus its margin.
senses.exampleCN: 置信区间就是估计值加减这段幅度。
senses.why: The interval is a point with two arms, and the arms carry the uncertainty the point cannot carry alone.
senses.whyCN: 区间是一个带两条臂的点，两条臂承载着点无法独自承载的不确定性。

senses.title: An interval for a difference
senses.definition: a range for the difference between two groups, used to judge whether the difference could plausibly be zero
senses.definitionCN: 两组差值所在的区间，用来判断差值是否可能为零
senses.example: The confidence interval for the difference included zero, so the effect was not established.
senses.exampleCN: 差值的置信区间包含零，因此效应尚未确立。
senses.why: A difference is itself an estimate, and its interval shows which directions and sizes remain plausible.
senses.whyCN: 差值本身也是一个估计，它的区间显示哪些方向与大小仍然可能。

senses.title: Interval versus credible interval
senses.titleCN: 置信区间与可信区间的区别
senses.definition: the contrast between a frequentist coverage interval and a Bayesian interval that carries a posterior probability
senses.definitionCN: 频率学派的覆盖率区间与带有后验概率的贝叶斯区间之间的对照
senses.example: A Bayesian credible interval answers a question that a confidence interval does not.
senses.exampleCN: 贝叶斯可信区间回答了一个置信区间不回答的问题。
senses.why: The two intervals can look alike on the page, but their probabilities are attached to different objects.
senses.whyCN: 两种区间在纸面上可能相似，但它们的概率附着在不同对象上。

senses.title: Width as a measure of precision
senses.definition: the way a narrower interval indicates a more precise estimate, usually because of a larger sample or less variation
senses.definitionCN: 区间越窄表示估计越精确，通常因为样本更大或变异更小
senses.example: The confidence interval narrowed after the second wave of data collection.
senses.exampleCN: 第二轮数据收集之后，置信区间变窄了。
senses.why: Width is the visible form of precision, and precision is bought with information.
senses.whyCN: 宽度是精确度的可见形式，而精确度是用信息换来的。

senses.title: Reading overlap between intervals
senses.definition: the practice of comparing two intervals to judge the plausibility of a difference, with care about what overlap does and does not prove
senses.definitionCN: 比较两个区间以判断差值是否可能，并注意重叠能证明什么、不能证明什么
senses.example: Overlapping confidence intervals do not by themselves prove that there is no difference.
senses.exampleCN: 置信区间重叠本身并不证明没有差异。
senses.why: Two wide intervals may overlap while the difference between their centres remains real.
senses.whyCN: 两个宽区间可以重叠，而它们中心之间的差异仍然真实存在。

intro.en: Confidence interval joins confidence, from Latin confidere, to trust fully, to interval, from Latin intervallum, the space between ramparts.
intro.cn: 这个术语把来自拉丁语 confidere「完全信任」的 confidence，与来自拉丁语 intervallum「城墙之间的空地」的 interval 组合起来。

items.en: Confidere meant to trust completely, from con- fully and fidere to trust.
items.cn: confidere 意为完全信任，由 con-「完全」与 fidere「信任」构成。

items.en: Confidentia named assurance or boldness, and English took it as confidence.
items.cn: confidentia 指确信或胆量，英语借入为 confidence。

items.en: Vallum meant a rampart or wall, and intervallum named the ground between two walls.
items.cn: vallum 指城墙或壁垒，intervallum 指两道墙之间的空地。

items.en: The noun widened from a space between walls to any gap in time or space.
items.cn: 这个名词从「墙间空地」扩展到时间或空间中的任何间隔。

items.en: English used interval for a gap and later for a set of values between two limits; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语用 interval 指间隔，后来指两个界限之间的一组取值；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Twentieth-century statistics joined the two nouns for a procedure-based range, and the exact origin of the phrase is debated.
items.cn: 二十世纪统计学把这两个名词组合成一种基于程序的区间，这个短语的确切起源仍有争议。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like confidence interval; the second group names neighbouring quantities in estimation.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 confidence interval 相近；第二组是与「估计量」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: Trust or assurance in a procedure or person.
entries.definitionCN: 指对程序或人的信任与把握。

entries.definition: Feeling sure about something.
entries.definitionCN: 指对某事感到有把握。

entries.definition: To trust someone with private information.
entries.definitionCN: 指把私密信息托付给某人。

entries.definition: A gap, or a set of values between two limits.
entries.definitionCN: 指间隔，或两界限之间的一组取值。

entries.definition: To come between; it looks close but its root is venire, to come.
entries.definitionCN: 指介入其间；形近但词根是 venire「来」。

entries.definition: The standard deviation of an estimate across repeated samples.
entries.definitionCN: 指估计量在反复抽样中的标准差。

entries.definition: A Bayesian range carrying a posterior probability.
entries.definitionCN: 指带有后验概率的贝叶斯区间。

entries.definition: The half-width of a survey interval around an estimate.
entries.definitionCN: 指调查中估计值两侧区间的半宽。

entries.definition: A single value used to estimate a parameter.
entries.definitionCN: 指用来估计参数的单个值。

entries.definition: The difference between the largest and smallest observed values.
entries.definitionCN: 指观测值中最大值与最小值之差。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations work through the real parts, word family and common phrases behind this term.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想依托这个术语背后真实的构词部件、同族词与常见搭配。

normal.en: Confidence is trust, and interval is the ground between two walls, so the phrase names a trusted space between two limits.
normal.cn: 「信心」是信任，「区间」是两墙之间的空地，这个短语指两条界限之间一块受信任的空间。

normal.en: Ninety-five per cent confidence means the procedure covers the truth in ninety-five per cent of repeated samples.
normal.cn: 百分之九十五置信意味着这套程序在反复抽样中百分之九十五的情况下盖住真值。

normal.en: A wider interval is more confident and less precise at the same time.
normal.cn: 更宽的区间同时更自信也更不精确。

normal.en: An interval that includes zero leaves the possibility of no difference open.
normal.cn: 包含零的区间使「没有差异」这一可能保持开放。

normal.en: A credible interval and a confidence interval can share a shape but not a meaning.
normal.cn: 可信区间与置信区间可以形状相同，含义却不同。

abstract.en: An interval is a net thrown around an unknown fish, and confidence describes the net, not the fish.
abstract.cn: 区间是撒向未知之鱼的一张网，信心描述的是网，而不是鱼。

abstract.en: The single number is a dot; the interval is the shadow the dot casts when uncertainty is the light.
abstract.cn: 单个数字是一个点，区间是当不确定性成为光源时那个点投下的影子。

abstract.en: Two intervals may overlap like two conversations in a corridor, without either speaker agreeing.
abstract.cn: 两个区间可以像走廊里的两段对话那样重叠，而两位说话者并未达成一致。

examples.en: The paper reports a confidence interval for every estimated coefficient.
examples.cn: 论文为每个估计系数报告了置信区间。

examples.en: A confidence interval that includes zero suggests the effect may be absent.
examples.cn: 包含零的置信区间提示效应可能不存在。

examples.en: The confidence interval was wide because the sample was small.
examples.cn: 由于样本小，置信区间很宽。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「置信」加「区间」——一个点不够，给它左右各伸一条臂，圈出一个可能范围：置信区间。

root: 拉丁 confidere「完全信任」← con-「完全」+ fidere「信任」→ confidentia → 英语 confidence；拉丁 vallum「城墙」→ intervallum「墙间空地」→ 英语 interval；二十世纪统计学把两者组合为置信区间。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from construction to reading: the range around an estimate, long-run coverage, the confidence level, the margin, intervals for differences, the contrast with credible intervals, width as precision, and the reading of overlap.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从构造走向解读：围绕估计值的区间、长期覆盖率、置信水平、两侧幅度、差值区间、与可信区间的区别、宽度即精确度，以及区间重叠的解读。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a horizontal axis with a point in the middle, arms extending both ways, and a bracket closing around the arms.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条横轴，中间一个点，左右各伸出一条臂，一只括号把两条臂围住。

branches.en: THE BUILT RANGE: an estimate with two arms, each arm carrying uncertainty.
branches.cn: 构造的范围：一个带两条臂的估计，每条臂承载不确定性。

branches.en: THE PROCEDURE'S PROMISE: long-run coverage, and the confidence level that states it.
branches.cn: 程序的承诺：长期覆盖率，以及陈述它的置信水平。

branches.en: THE DIFFERENCE: an interval that can include zero and leave no effect established.
branches.cn: 差值：一个可以包含零、使效应无法确立的区间。

branches.en: THE ALTERNATIVE AND THE PRECISION: a Bayesian interval beside it, and width as visible precision.
branches.cn: 替代与精确：旁边的贝叶斯区间，以及作为可见精确度的宽度。

branches.en: THE COMPARISON: overlap read with care about what it does not prove.
branches.cn: 比较：谨慎解读重叠不能证明什么。

definition_zh: 测高仪；高度计；（飞机上的）高度表
definition_en: an instrument that measures altitude, especially the height of an aircraft above a level
core_image: 驾驶舱里一格格转动的指针，告诉你离地多高
scene: 飞行员爬升时盯着表盘。 The pilot checked the altimeter at ten thousand feet.
sceneCN: 这里的 altimeter 是「高度表」（第 1 个义项：测量高度的仪器）；句意是飞行员在一万英尺处查看高度表。

derivatives.zh: 同根名词，义为「高度；海拔」

senses.title: An aircraft height gauge
senses.definition: the cockpit instrument showing an aircraft's height above a reference level
senses.definitionCN: 座舱内显示飞机相对于基准面高度的仪表
senses.example: The altimeter read nine thousand feet.
senses.exampleCN: 高度表读数为九千英尺。
senses.why: Built from altus "high" plus metron "measure": the high-measurer.
senses.whyCN: 由 altus「高」加 metron「测量」构成：测量高的仪器。

senses.title: A barometric altimeter
senses.definition: an altimeter that converts air pressure into altitude
senses.definitionCN: 把气压换算成高度的测高仪
senses.example: Climbers carry a barometric altimeter uphill.
senses.exampleCN: 登山者背着气压高度计上山。
senses.why: Air thins with height, so pressure becomes a height signal.
senses.whyCN: 空气随高度变稀，气压因此成为高度信号。

senses.title: A radar or laser altimeter
senses.definition: a device measuring height by reflected radio waves or laser light
senses.definitionCN: 以反射无线电波或激光测高的装置
senses.example: The satellite's radar altimeter mapped the sea surface.
senses.exampleCN: 卫星的雷达测高仪测绘了海面。
senses.why: Timing a signal's round trip yields the distance below.
senses.whyCN: 信号往返的时间差给出下方距离。

senses.title: A surveying or scientific altimeter
senses.definition: a precision instrument for measuring elevations in field science
senses.definitionCN: 野外科学中测量海拔的精密仪器
senses.example: The team logged each site with an altimeter.
senses.exampleCN: 考察队用测高仪记录每个站点。
senses.why: Wherever height matters, a measuring instrument follows.
senses.whyCN: 凡高度要紧之处，测量仪器随之出现。

senses.title: A watch or wearable altimeter
senses.definition: an altimeter function built into watches or phones
senses.definitionCN: 集成于腕表或手机的高度计功能
senses.example: His watch has an altimeter for hiking.
senses.exampleCN: 他的手表带徒步用的高度计。
senses.why: Sensors shrink; the instrument becomes a feature.
senses.whyCN: 传感器缩小，仪器变成了功能。

senses.title: The system or discipline of height measurement
senses.definition: altimeter used broadly for a measuring system of altitude
senses.definitionCN: 泛指测量高度的系统或方法
senses.example: The probe's altimeter failed before landing.
senses.exampleCN: 探测器的测高系统在着陆前失灵。
senses.why: The word can name the whole apparatus, not just one dial.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可指整套装置，不只是一个表盘。

senses.title: Altitude data as output
senses.definition: the reading or data stream produced by an altimeter
senses.definitionCN: 测高仪产生的读数或数据流
senses.example: We lost altimeter data during the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨中我们丢失了测高数据。
senses.why: Instrument names often extend to their outputs.
senses.whyCN: 仪器名常转指其输出。

senses.title: Figurative: a gauge of level or status
senses.definition: used figuratively for anything that indicates how high or advanced something is
senses.definitionCN: 喻指显示事物高度或先进程度的标志
senses.example: Stock prices are the market's altimeter.
senses.exampleCN: 股价是市场的晴雨高度表。
senses.why: A meter of height measures success or progress by metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 测高的仪表借喻度量成就或进展。

examples.cn: 她的测高仪显示峰顶为 6900 米。

examples.en: The rocket's altimeter triggered the parachute.
examples.cn: 火箭的测高仪触发了降落伞。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥提米特」——奥提（alti）摸高、米特（meter）量尺，摸高量尺就是高度表。

root: 拉丁语 altus「高的」（印欧词根 *al-「生长」）+ 希腊语 metron「量度」词形 -meter「测量器」；十八九世纪科学造词，二十世纪初随飞行成为航空标准词。

sensesIntro.en: Starting with the cockpit gauge, the instrument diversifies into barometric, radar, surveying, and wearable forms, then extends to the whole system, its data output, and a metaphor for level.
sensesIntro.cn: 从座舱仪表出发，仪器分化为气压式、雷达式、测绘式与可穿戴式，继而扩展到整套系统、数据输出与喻义标尺。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dial that turns height into numbers
core.cn: 核心意象：把高度变成数字的表盘

branches.en: The aircraft gauge at the core.
branches.cn: 核心的航空仪表。

branches.en: Barometric and radar/laser measuring principles.
branches.cn: 气压式与雷达/激光测高原理。

branches.en: Field science and wearable forms.
branches.cn: 野外科学与可穿戴形式。

branches.en: The whole measuring system.
branches.cn: 整套测量系统。

branches.en: Data output and the figurative gauge.
branches.cn: 数据输出与喻义标尺。

intro.en: Altimeter is a textbook alti- + -meter compound.
intro.cn: altimeter 是典型的 alti- 加 -meter 复合词。

latinIntro.en: The blend joins a Latin adjective base to a Greek measuring suffix.
latinIntro.cn: 该词把拉丁形容词词基与希腊测量后缀结合。

definition_zh: 掺假；使不纯；败坏
definition_en: to make something impure or lower in quality by adding another substance
core_image: 一滴墨汁落进清水瓶，整瓶水再也回不到从前
scene: 作坊老板背对着门，把便宜油倒进贵油罐。 The merchant adulterated the olive oil with cheap rapeseed oil.
sceneCN: 这里 adulterate 是「掺假、使不纯」（第 1 个义项：往好东西里混入次等物）；句意为商人往橄榄油里掺了廉价的菜籽油。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「掺假；掺杂」
由动词派生的施动名词，义为「掺杂物」
由动词加施动后缀构成，义为「掺假者」

senses.title: Make goods impure by mixing
senses.definition: to lower the quality of food, drink or goods by adding inferior substances
senses.definitionCN: 往食品、饮品或货物里加入次等物质以降低其品质
senses.example: The merchant adulterated the olive oil with cheap rapeseed oil.
senses.exampleCN: 商人往橄榄油里掺了廉价的菜籽油。
senses.why: Latin adulterare means 'to pollute', so the core image is corrupting something clean by pouring into it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 adulterare 意为「污染」，核心意象就是往干净东西里灌入脏东西。

senses.title: Corrupt something abstract
senses.definition: to weaken or spoil the purity of an idea, language or tradition
senses.definitionCN: 使观念、语言或传统失去纯粹
senses.example: Critics said the sequel adulterated the spirit of the original film.
senses.exampleCN: 评论者说续集败坏了原作的精神。
senses.why: Mixing inferior matter extends by metaphor to ideas: the pure original gets watered down.
senses.whyCN: 掺次等物的动作经隐喻引申到观念：纯粹的原型被稀释。

senses.title: Adjective: impure, debased
senses.definition: describing something that has been made impure or of lower quality
senses.definitionCN: 形容已被掺假或品质下降的东西
senses.example: The customs office seized sacks of adulterate saffron.
senses.exampleCN: 海关查获了几袋掺假藏红花。
senses.why: The past participle hardens into an adjective: the result-state of the verb.
senses.whyCN: 过去分词凝固为形容词：动词造成的结果状态。

intro.en: Adulterate comes from Latin adulterare, 'to pollute, to corrupt', built on adulter, 'spurious, impure'.
intro.cn: adulterate 来自拉丁语 adulterare（污染、败坏），词根是 adulter（假的、不纯的）。

items.en: The root adulter described anything spurious, mixed, or not what it claimed to be.
items.cn: 词根 adulter 形容一切假冒的、掺混的、名不副实的东西。

items.en: Adulterare was the verb 'to corrupt'; ancient writers used it of wine, metals and morals alike.
items.cn: 动词 adulterare 意为「败坏」；古代作家用它形容酒、金属与道德。

items.en: English took the verb in the sixteenth century, first of corrupted goods.
items.cn: 英语于十六世纪借入该动词，最初用于被做手脚的货物。

items.en: The adjective use for 'impure' settled beside the verb.
items.cn: 十七世纪，「不纯的」形容词用法在动词旁定型。

items.en: Modern use stresses commercial fraud, with the adjective common in customs and lab reports.
items.cn: 现代用法强调商业欺诈，形容词常见于海关与化验报告。

note.en: The first group gathers words of similar shape; the second gathers near synonyms of corrupting and diluting.
note.cn: 第一组收词形相近的词；第二组收表示「败坏、稀释」的近义词。

entries.definition: A grown person; only the opening letters are shared, the roots differ.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成年人」；只是开头字母相同，词根不同。

entries.definition: Marital unfaithfulness; from the same Latin adulter, corrupted fidelity rather than corrupted goods.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「通奸」；出自同一拉丁词根 adulter，是「被败坏的忠诚」而非「被败坏的货物」。

entries.definition: Excessive flattery; close in sound, unrelated in root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「吹捧」；发音接近，词源无关。

entries.definition: To make something dirty or unsafe, often by accident.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「污染」，多指无意间弄脏。

entries.definition: To lower the value or status of something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「贬低；使劣化」，偏重价值与地位。

entries.definition: To weaken by mixing with water or another thinning agent.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「稀释；冲淡」，是掺假的一种具体方式。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the pollute root and the oil-seller scene; the abstract hooks picture ink in water and a lowered grade.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「污染」词根与卖油人场景；抽象记忆点想象水中的墨与降级的货。

normal.en: Latin adulterare means 'to pollute'.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 adulterare 意为「污染」。

normal.en: Adulterant is the thing, adulterate the act.
normal.cn: adulterant 是物，adulterate 是行为。

normal.en: Adulteration is the crime's name in law.
normal.cn: adulteration 是法律上这种罪行的名字。

normal.en: Adulterated goods fail customs tests.
normal.cn: 掺假货物过不了海关检验。

normal.en: Adultery shares the root but means unfaithfulness.
normal.cn: adultery 同根但指不忠。

abstract.en: Picture ink spreading through a bottle of clear water.
abstract.cn: 想象墨汁在一瓶清水里晕开。

abstract.en: Picture gold coins shaved and refilled with copper.
abstract.cn: 想象金币被削去一角补上铜。

abstract.en: Picture a recipe ruined by one cheap shortcut.
abstract.cn: 想象一道菜谱被一个廉价的偷工步骤毁掉。

examples.en: The merchant adulterated the olive oil with cheap rapeseed oil.
examples.cn: 商人往橄榄油里掺了廉价的菜籽油。

examples.en: It is illegal to adulterate milk with water for sale.
examples.cn: 往牛奶里掺水出售是违法的。

examples.en: Years of careless edits adulterated the original text.
examples.cn: 多年草率的编辑败坏了原文。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额特喂」——额外地喂进去一些假料，好东西就被败坏了。

root: 拉丁语 adulter（假的、不纯的）→ adulterare（污染、败坏）→ 英语 adulterate；核心义是「把干净的弄脏、把纯的变假」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from mixing impurities into goods, to corrupting abstract things, to the adjective for the result.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项从给货物掺假，到败坏抽象事物，再到形容结果的形容词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drop of ink falling into clear water
core.cn: 核心意象：落入清水的一滴墨

branches.en: Goods spoiled by what was slipped into them.
branches.cn: 被偷偷混入的次等物毁掉的货物。

branches.en: Ideas and traditions watered down.
branches.cn: 被稀释变味的观念与传统。

branches.en: The finished state: already impure.
branches.cn: 完成时的状态：已然不纯。

branches.en: Both senses trade purity for cheapness.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在用纯度换廉价。

branches.en: Customs and labs test for it daily.
branches.cn: 海关与化验室天天检验它。

intro.en: The word carries the Latin pollute root adulter- with the verb ending -ate, and the family gives adulteration and adulterant.
intro.cn: 这个词带着拉丁语「污染」词根 adulter- 与动词尾 -ate，同族词有 adulteration 与 adulterant。

latinIntro.en: Latin adulter and adulterare are the recorded ancestors.
latinIntro.cn: 这里记录的拉丁语 adulter 与 adulterare 是直接祖先。

definition_zh: 青少年；青春期的；不成熟的
definition_en: a young person between childhood and adulthood, or relating to that stage of life
core_image: 一个正在长个子的少年，袖子短了一截，声音也变低了
scene: 他一年长了十厘米，鞋码换了两次，说话却还是吞吞吐吐。 The adolescent boy stood awkwardly at the door.
sceneCN: 这里的 adolescent 是「青春期的」（第 2 个义项：属于少年阶段的）；句意是那个青春期的男孩局促地站在门口。

pos.zh: 形容词：青春期的；不成熟的

derivatives.zh: 由词干加名词后缀构成，义为「青春期；少年时代」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「以少年的方式」（罕用）

senses.title: A young person growing up
senses.definition: a person who is no longer a child but not yet an adult
senses.definitionCN: 已经不再是儿童、但尚未成为成年人的人
senses.example: Many adolescents struggle with lack of sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 许多青少年饱受睡眠不足之苦。
senses.why: Latin adolescere means to grow up, and its participle names the one who is in the middle of that growing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 adolescere 意为「长大」，它的分词就指正处在这一成长过程中的人。

senses.title: Relating to the teenage stage
senses.definition: connected with the period of life between childhood and adulthood
senses.definitionCN: 与童年与成年之间那个人生阶段有关的
senses.example: The clinic offers advice to adolescent patients.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所为青少年病人提供建议。
senses.why: The same participle also works as an adjective, describing anything that belongs to that stretch of growing up.
senses.whyCN: 同一个分词也能作形容词，描述属于那段成长时期的一切。

senses.title: Immature in manner
senses.definition: behaving in a way that seems immature for one's age
senses.definitionCN: 行为方式相对于年龄显得不够成熟
senses.example: His adolescent humour annoyed the older staff.
senses.exampleCN: 他那套幼稚的幽默让年长的同事很烦。
senses.why: Because the stage is halfway to adulthood, the adjective can be used to criticise behaviour that has not finished growing.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个阶段只走到成年的一半，形容词便可用来批评尚未「长成」的行为。

intro.en: The word names a person in the middle of growing up.
intro.cn: 这个词指一个正处在成长中途的人。

items.en: alescere was an inchoative verb meaning to begin to grow.
items.cn: alescere 是表示「开始生长」的起始动词。

items.en: ad- plus alescere formed adolescere, to grow up, to come to maturity.
items.cn: ad- 加 alescere 构成 adolescere，意为「长大、成熟起来」。

items.en: The present participle adolescens named a young person still growing.
items.cn: 现在分词 adolescens 指仍在成长的年轻人。

items.en: French passed the adjective and noun into English in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 法语在十五世纪把这个形容词与名词一并传入英语。

items.en: Medicine and psychology gave the word a precise age range and a set of typical problems.
items.cn: 医学与心理学给这个词划定了大致年龄范围，并附上一组典型问题。

note.en: The first group shares the growing root; the second gathers words for young people.
note.cn: 第一组共享「生长」词根；第二组收指年轻人的词。

entries.definition: the stage of growing up
entries.definitionCN: 青春期

entries.definition: in a teenage manner
entries.definitionCN: 以少年的方式

entries.definition: a fully grown person
entries.definitionCN: 成年人

entries.definition: a person aged thirteen to nineteen
entries.definitionCN: 十几岁的青少年

entries.definition: young, or a young person
entries.definitionCN: 少年的

entries.definition: having the qualities of youth
entries.definitionCN: 年轻的

entries.definition: not yet fully developed
entries.definitionCN: 不成熟的

normalIntro.en: The ending -escent marks a process in progress.
normalIntro.cn: 词尾 -escent 标记一个正在进行的过程。

normal.en: adolescere means to grow up, so an adolescent is one still growing.
normal.cn: adolescere 意为长大，所以 adolescent 是「还在长」的人。

normal.en: The noun for the stage is adolescence, with -ence instead of -ent.
normal.cn: 表示「阶段」的名词是 adolescence，词尾换成 -ence。

normal.en: adolescent health and adolescent development are standard phrases in reports.
normal.cn: adolescent health 与 adolescent development 是报告里的固定说法。

normal.en: The word can be a noun or an adjective without changing form.
normal.cn: 这个词作名词或形容词时形式不变。

normal.en: Keep the c: adolescent, not adolesent.
normal.cn: 别漏掉 c：是 adolescent，不是 adolesent。

abstract.en: See a boy whose sleeves have grown too short.
abstract.cn: 想象一个男孩，袖子已经短了一截。

abstract.en: Picture a voice cracking in the middle of a sentence.
abstract.cn: 想象说话说到一半忽然破音。

abstract.en: Think of shoes bought twice in one year.
abstract.cn: 想象一年里买了两次鞋。

examples.en: Many adolescents struggle with lack of sleep.
examples.cn: 许多青少年饱受睡眠不足之苦。

examples.en: Adolescent behaviour can be hard for parents to read.
examples.cn: 青少年的行为有时让父母难以理解。

examples.en: The clinic offers advice to adolescent patients.
examples.cn: 这家诊所为青少年病人提供建议。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额的勒森特」——额头上写着勒森特的名字，因为他正处在长个子的年纪。

root: 拉丁语 adolescere（长大），由 ad-（向）与 alescere（开始生长）构成；分词 adolescens 指「正在长大的人」，即青少年。

sensesIntro.en: The same word names the young person, the stage and the immaturity.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个词，既指年轻人，也指那个阶段与那份不成熟。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body outgrowing its clothes.
core.cn: 核心意象：身体长得比衣服快。

branches.en: a pupil who is neither child nor adult
branches.cn: 既不是孩子也不是大人的学生

branches.en: a clinic built for teenage patients
branches.cn: 为少年病人设立的诊所

branches.en: the years when the voice changes
branches.cn: 嗓音变化的那些年

branches.en: a joke that is too young for the room
branches.cn: 在场合里显得太稚嫩的笑话

branches.en: the stage and the immaturity it is blamed for
branches.cn: 这个阶段与它因此被责怪的不成熟

intro.en: A prefix of direction and a root of growing, with a participle ending.
intro.cn: 方向词头、表示生长的词根，再加一个分词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The -esc- element marks a process beginning, as in convalescent.
latinIntro.cn: -esc- 这一成分标记「开始的过程」，convalescent 亦然。

definition_zh: 令人不快的；不舒服的；不客气的；使人为难的
definition_en: not enjoyable or comfortable, or rude and unfriendly
core_image: 刚端起汤碗就闻到一股馊味
scene: 公交车在雨天挤得满当当，有人把滴着水的伞搁在别人裤脚上。 The damp smell made the ride distinctly unpleasant.
sceneCN: 这里 unpleasant 是「令人不快的」（第 1 个义项：让人不舒服、不愉快）；句意为潮湿的气味让这趟车程明显令人难受。端起汤碗闻到馊味的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「令人不快地；不客气地」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「不愉快；不快之事」
去掉否定前缀后的肯定形式，义为「令人愉快的」
同源动词，义为「使高兴；取悦」

senses.title: Something that is not enjoyable to the senses
senses.definition: not enjoyable to see, hear, smell, or touch
senses.definitionCN: 在视觉、听觉、嗅觉或触觉上让人难受
senses.example: There was an unpleasant smell from the drain.
senses.exampleCN: 下水道里冒出一股难闻的气味。
senses.why: The prefix means not and the base means pleasing, so the word starts as simply the negative of pleasant.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 un- 表示「不」，词根本义是「令人愉快的」，因此这个词起初就是 pleasant 的反面。

senses.title: Something bad that arrives without warning
senses.definition: used of news, surprises, or events that one would rather not have
senses.definitionCN: 形容人们宁可不发生的消息、意外或事件
senses.example: The test results came as an unpleasant surprise.
senses.exampleCN: 检验结果成了一个不愉快的意外。
senses.why: Anything that spoils pleasure is unpleasant, and bad news spoils it in one stroke.
senses.whyCN: 凡是把愉悦一扫而空的东西就是令人不快的，坏消息正是一下子把它扫空。

senses.title: A person who is rude or hard to deal with
senses.definition: used of a person whose manner is rude or unkind
senses.definitionCN: 形容说话行事无礼、刻薄的人
senses.example: The clerk was unpleasant to the old man at the counter.
senses.exampleCN: 柜台后的店员对那位老人很不客气。
senses.why: A person's manner of displeasing others is named by the same adjective that names the experience.
senses.whyCN: 一个人让别人不痛快的那种态度，也用同一个形容词来命名。

senses.title: A task or duty that one dreads
senses.definition: used of work that is boring, dirty, or upsetting
senses.definitionCN: 形容无聊、肮脏或令人难受的工作
senses.example: Cleaning the drains is an unpleasant task nobody volunteers for.
senses.exampleCN: 清理下水道是件没人主动愿意干的烦人活。
senses.why: Duty has no smell, yet it can be felt as the same sourness in the nose from the core image.
senses.whyCN: 职责本身没有气味，但做起来时鼻子里的那股酸味是一样的。

senses.title: An awkward situation that embarrasses people
senses.definition: used of situations that make those involved feel awkward
senses.definitionCN: 形容让在场的人都感到尴尬的处境
senses.example: Asking about the money put her in an unpleasant position.
senses.exampleCN: 问起那笔钱让她陷入很为难的处境。
senses.why: When an external thing causes inner discomfort, the discomfort moves into the situation itself.
senses.whyCN: 当外物带出内心不适时，这种不适就转移到了处境本身。

intro.en: Another plain negative compound, this time over an adjective that descends from Latin placere, to please.
intro.cn: 又一个朴素的否定复合词，这次压在源自拉丁语 placere（使高兴）的形容词之上。

items.en: The native prefix un- is added to borrowings to reverse their meaning.
items.cn: 本土前缀 un- 被加到借词上以反转其词义。

items.en: Placere meant to please or to be acceptable, with the adjective placidus, calm and pleasing.
items.cn: placere 意为「取悦、被接受」，形容词 placidus 意为「平和的、可喜的」。

items.en: Plaire brought the verb into French, and the present participle plaisant meant pleasing.
items.cn: plaire 把这个动词带入法语，现在分词 plaisant 意为「令人愉快的」。

items.en: Pleasant enters English from the French participle and describes what gives pleasure.
items.cn: pleasant 由这个法语分词进入英语，用来形容给人愉快的事物。

items.en: Unpleasant is formed by the negative prefix and extends from smells to people and duties.
items.cn: unpleasant 由否定前缀构成，并从气味扩展到人物与职责。

items.en: Its noun unpleasantness later becomes a polite word for a quarrel or an awkward scene.
items.cn: 其名词形式 unpleasantness 后来成为争吵或尴尬场面的委婉说法。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the please family, and the near-meaning group collects words for what we dislike.
note.cn: 形近组沿着 please 词族展开，近义组汇集表示令人嫌恶的词。

entries.definition: enjoyable and giving pleasure
entries.definitionCN: 令人愉快的

entries.definition: in a way that is not enjoyable
entries.definitionCN: 令人不快地

entries.definition: an awkward or quarrelsome situation
entries.definitionCN: 不快之事；别扭

entries.definition: to make someone happy
entries.definitionCN: 使高兴；取悦

entries.definition: a feeling of enjoyment

normalIntro.en: Everything about the word is familiar: an everyday negative prefix over the ordinary word for pleasure.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词的一切都很熟悉：日常的否定前缀压在日常表示愉悦的词上。

normal.en: Un- plus pleasant: the negative is taken directly from the positive.
normal.cn: un- 加 pleasant：否定直接取自肯定形式。

normal.en: An unpleasant smell and an unpleasant surprise cover the two most common collocations.
normal.cn: an unpleasant smell 与 an unpleasant surprise 覆盖了最常见的两类搭配。

normal.en: The adverb unpleasantly is used mainly of weather, sounds, and smells.
normal.cn: 副词 unpleasantly 主要用于天气、声音和气味。

normal.en: The noun unpleasantness often means a quarrel rather than a feeling.
normal.cn: 名词 unpleasantness 常指一场争执，而不是一种感受。

normal.en: Pleasant, please, and pleasure share the Latin root placere.
normal.cn: pleasant、please、pleasure 共享拉丁词根 placere。

abstract.en: Smell soup that has stood too long in a warm kitchen.
abstract.cn: 闻一碗在热厨房里放久了的汤。

abstract.en: Sit beside a passenger whose wet umbrella drips on your shoe.
abstract.cn: 坐在一位湿伞往你鞋上滴水的乘客旁边。

abstract.en: Watch a room go quiet after someone asks the wrong question.
abstract.cn: 看一个房间在有人问错问题之后安静下来。

examples.en: An unpleasant smell came from the rubbish bin behind the kitchen.
examples.cn: 厨房后面的垃圾桶里冒出一股难闻的气味。

examples.en: He was asked to stay calm even when the customer was unpleasant to him.
examples.cn: 即使顾客对他很不客气，他也被要求保持冷静。

examples.en: Cleaning the cellar is an unpleasant task, but somebody must do it.
examples.cn: 清理地窖是件烦人的活，但总得有人干。

core.cn: 核心意象：扑到鼻子里、把胃口赶跑的一股气味。

branches.en: The sensory branch: what offends smell, ear, or eye.
branches.cn: 感官分支：冲撞嗅觉、听觉或视觉之物。

branches.en: The news branch: the surprise nobody wanted.
branches.cn: 消息分支：谁都不想收到的意外。

branches.en: The person branch: manner that makes others wince.
branches.cn: 人物分支：让别人皱眉的态度。

branches.en: The duty branch: work that is dirty or dull.
branches.cn: 职责分支：又脏又闷的工作。

branches.en: The situation branch: a scene that leaves everyone stuck.
branches.cn: 处境分支：让所有人都僵住的一幕。

definition_zh: 迁移；移居；迁徙；移民潮；数据迁移；细胞迁移；污染物迁移；劳动力流动；系统间转移
definition_en: the movement of people, animals or other things from one place, region or system to another, especially over a long distance or in large numbers
core_image: 暮色中一群鸟排成人字，从一片湿地飞向另一片湿地
scene: 这里指「迁移」。 At dusk the birds form a wedge and leave one marsh for another: their movement is migration.
sceneCN: 这里 migration 是「迁徙」（第 2 个义项：动物迁徙）；句意：暮色中鸟群排成人字，离开一片湿地飞向另一片湿地，它们的移动就是迁徙。图中可辨识物件：人字形鸟群、起飞的湿地、远处的湿地、暮色天空、芦苇。

pos.zh: 迁移；移居；迁徙；移民潮；数据迁移

forms.label: 单数（一次迁移或迁移这件事）
复数（多批迁移或多条迁徙路线）

senses.title: People moving to a new place to live
senses.titleCN: 人的迁移：搬到另一处生活
senses.definition: the movement of people from one place or country to another in order to settle there
senses.definitionCN: 人们从一个地方或国家移到另一个地方或国家定居
senses.example: Migration from the countryside to the cities changed the labour market.
senses.exampleCN: 从乡村向城市的迁移改变了劳动力市场。
senses.why: Latin migrare means to move from one place to another, and migratio names that moving. Applied to people, the change of place becomes a change of home.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 migrare 意为从一处移到另一处，migratio 指这一移动。用在人身上，换地方就变成了换家。

senses.title: Animal migration: seasonal movement between regions
senses.titleCN: 动物迁徙：随季节在区域间移动
senses.definition: the seasonal movement of animals, birds or fish from one region to another and often back again
senses.definitionCN: 动物、鸟类或鱼类随季节从一个地区移到另一地区，且常常再返回
senses.example: The migration of the geese follows the river valley every autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 每年秋天雁群的迁徙都沿着河谷走。
senses.why: The same verb fits animals because they also leave one place for another. The word adds nothing about distance; the round trip and the season are supplied by context.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词也适用于动物，因为它们同样离开一处去另一处。词本身不涉及距离；往返与季节是由语境提供的。

senses.title: A wave of movement: numbers on the move
senses.definition: a large-scale movement of people or animals considered as a quantity or a trend
senses.definitionCN: 被当作数量或趋势来看待的大规模人潮或兽群移动
senses.example: The century saw a migration of millions across the border.
senses.exampleCN: 那个世纪有数百万人越过边境迁移。
senses.why: Once many journeys are counted together, migration stops being one person's move and becomes a demographic event, measured and graphed by agencies.
senses.whyCN: 当许多趟行程被一起计数，migration 就不再是一个人的搬家，而成为一个人口事件，被机构测量并绘成图表。

senses.title: Data migration: moving information between systems
senses.titleCN: 数据迁移：把信息搬到另一套系统
senses.definition: the transfer of data from one storage system, format or platform to another
senses.definitionCN: 把数据从一种存储系统、格式或平台转移到另一种
senses.example: The data migration took three nights and two rollbacks.
senses.exampleCN: 这次数据迁移用了三个夜晚和两次回滚。
senses.why: Computing keeps the literal image: records that lived in one place are moved to another. The risk is the same as in any move, that something is lost on the way.
senses.whyCN: 计算机领域保留了字面意象：原本住在一处的记录被搬到另一处。风险也跟任何搬家一样：路上可能丢东西。

senses.title: Cell migration: cells moving through tissue
senses.titleCN: 细胞迁移：细胞在组织中移动
senses.definition: in biology, the directed movement of cells through tissue, as in wound healing or development
senses.definitionCN: 生物学中指细胞在组织中定向移动，如伤口愈合或发育过程中的移动
senses.example: Cell migration is central to how wounds close.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞迁移是伤口如何闭合的核心环节。
senses.why: Biology applies the word at a scale invisible to the eye. A cell leaves one position for another, so the same migrare serves, with the 'journey' compressed to micrometres.
senses.whyCN: 生物学把这个词用在肉眼不可见的尺度。细胞离开一个位置去另一个位置，所以同一个 migrare 仍然适用，只是「行程」被压缩到微米级。

senses.title: Pollutant migration: spreading through soil and water
senses.titleCN: 污染物迁移：在土壤与水中扩散
senses.definition: the movement of a substance, especially a pollutant, through soil, water or air
senses.definitionCN: 物质、尤指污染物在土壤、水或空气中的移动
senses.example: The study traced the migration of nitrates into the groundwater.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究追踪了硝酸盐向地下水的迁移。
senses.why: Here the mover is not a creature but a substance. The word still means a change of place, and the scientific use adds the question of how far and how fast.
senses.whyCN: 这里移动的不是生物，而是物质。词仍指换地方，科学用法则再加上「多远、多快」的问题。

senses.title: Labour migration: workers following demand
senses.titleCN: 劳动力迁移：工人跟着需求走
senses.definition: the movement of workers between regions or countries in search of employment
senses.definitionCN: 工人为寻找就业而在地区或国家之间移动
senses.example: Seasonal labour migration fills the harvest with hands.
senses.exampleCN: 季节性劳动力迁移为收割季节补足了人手。
senses.why: When the reason for moving is work, the word becomes an economic term. The same journey is now explained by wages rather than by home.
senses.whyCN: 当移动的原因是工作时，这个词就成了经济术语。同一趟行程，如今用工资来解释，而不是用家。

senses.title: Any transfer between systems
senses.titleCN: 一般迁移：在一个系统与另一个系统之间转移
senses.definition: a general transfer from one system, category or state to another
senses.definitionCN: 从一种系统、类别或状态转移到另一种的统称
senses.example: The migration of files from paper archives to digital ones took a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 把档案从纸质迁到数字形式用了一个年代。
senses.why: The general sense is simply 'a move from one container to another'. It keeps the word usable for archives, accounts, populations and species alike.
senses.whyCN: 一般义就是「从一个容器搬到另一个容器」。这使这个词能用于档案、账户、人口与物种。

intro.en: Migration comes from Latin migratio, the noun of migrare 'to move from one place to another'. English borrowed it in the 17th century, at first for the movement of people, and extended it to animals, cells and data in later centuries. The deeper link to a root meaning 'to change' is generally accepted but not certain. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: migration 出自拉丁语 migratio，即 migrare「从一处移到另一处」的名词。英语在 17 世纪借入，最初指人的迁移，后来几个世纪才扩展到动物、细胞与数据。它与一个意为「改变」的词根有更深联系，这一点一般认为成立，但并非确证。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Data migration and cell migration become standard phrases as computing and cell biology grow.
items.cn: 随着计算技术与细胞生物学的发展，data migration（数据迁移）与 cell migration（细胞迁移）成为固定说法。

items.en: The study of bird migration gives the word its popular natural-history sense.
items.cn: 对鸟类迁徙的研究赋予这个词流行的自然史含义。

items.en: English migration is recorded, naming the movement of people from one country or region to another.
items.cn: 英语 migration 见于记载，指人从一个国家或地区迁往另一个。

items.en: migratio is the noun of migrare; the same verb gives migrate, migrant, immigrate and emigrate.
items.cn: migratio 是 migrare 的名词；同一个动词给出 migrate、migrant、immigrate、emigrate。

items.en: A reconstructed root *mei- 'to change, go' is often proposed behind migrare, though the connection is generally accepted rather than proven.
items.cn: 常有人为 migrare 提出重构词根 *mei-「改变、行走」，但这一联系一般认为成立，而非已证明。

note.en: The first group separates the two prefixed relatives and one false friend; the second compares words for movement that differ in scale or cause.
note.cn: 第一组把两个带前缀的同族词和一个假朋友分开；第二组比较规模或成因不同的移动类词。

entries.definition: the act of leaving one's own country to settle elsewhere. The prefix e- 'out' fixes the point of view at the country of departure.
entries.definitionCN: 离开本国到别处定居的行为。前缀 e-「向外」把视角固定在出发国。

entries.definition: the act of coming into a country to settle. The prefix im- 'in' fixes the point of view at the receiving country, so the same journey is emigration or immigration depending on who is counting.
entries.definitionCN: 进入某国定居的行为。前缀 im-「向内」把视角固定在接收国，因此同一趟行程，看谁在计数，就或叫移出或叫移入。

entries.definition: a severe recurring headache. It comes through French from Greek hēmikrania 'half the skull', and has nothing to do with migrare despite the shared opening.
entries.definitionCN: 反复发作的剧烈头痛。它经法语来自希腊语 hēmikrania「半个头骨」，虽开头相同，却与 migrare 无关。

entries.definition: any change of position. It is the widest word, with no implication of settling, season or distance.
entries.definitionCN: 任何位置变化。它是最宽泛的词，不含定居、季节或距离的意味。

entries.definition: the act of moving a person, company or object to a new place. It is usually a single planned move, where migration suggests many moves or a recurring pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 把个人、公司或物件搬到新地点。它通常指一次有计划的搬迁，而 migration 暗示许多次移动或反复出现的模式。

entries.definition: the forcing of people from their homes by war, disaster or development. It stresses that the move was compelled, not chosen.
entries.definitionCN: 因战争、灾害或开发而被迫离开家园。它强调移动是被迫而非自愿。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real pieces of the word and its real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想只使用这个词真实的构成成分和真实同族词，不用编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: migrare means 'to move from one place to another'; every sense is that verb wearing a different subject.
normal.cn: migrare 意为「从一处移到另一处」；每个义项都是这个动词换了个主语。

normal.en: e- 'out' and im- 'in' split the family: emigration looks from the leaving side, immigration from the arriving side.
normal.cn: e-「向外」与 im-「向内」把这个词族分开：emigration 从离开方看，immigration 从到达方看。

normal.en: Migraine is not a relative: its Greek source means 'half the skull', not 'moving away'.
normal.cn: migraine 不是同族词：它的希腊来源意为「半个头骨」，而不是「迁走」。

normal.en: The -tion ending names the event, while migrant names the person who performs it.
normal.cn: -tion 词尾命名事件，而 migrant 命名实施这一行为的人。

normal.en: Data and cells migrate in the same grammatical way as birds: something leaves one place for another.
normal.cn: 数据与细胞的「迁移」在语法上和鸟一样：某物离开一处去另一处。

abstract.en: Picture a dotted line from one marsh to another, followed each year by a new generation.
abstract.cn: 想象一条从这片湿地连到那片湿地的虚线，每年由新一代沿着它飞。

abstract.en: Any migration has three parts: a place left, a route, and a place arrived at; every sense uses those three.
abstract.cn: 任何迁移都有三部分：离开的地方、路线、抵达的地方；每个义项都用到这三样。

abstract.en: The word never asks whether the move was good, only that it happened and in which direction.
abstract.cn: 这个词从不过问迁移好不好，只问它是否发生、朝哪个方向。

examples.en: Rural migration has emptied many mountain villages.
examples.cn: 乡村人口外迁让许多山村空了。

examples.en: The migration of monarch butterflies covers thousands of kilometres.
examples.cn: 帝王蝶的迁徙要跨越数千公里。

examples.en: The company scheduled the data migration for a weekend.
examples.cn: 公司把数据迁移安排在周末。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「买个雷神」——候鸟一路买个雷神当路标，年年迁往同一处 → migration 迁徙、迁移

root: 拉丁语 migrare「从一处移到另一处」→ migratio → 英语 migration。核心是「离开一处、沿路、抵达另一处」，主语可以是人、鸟、细胞、数据或污染物。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses keep one image: a dotted line from one place to another. What changes is who or what travels along it — settlers, birds, whole populations, records, cells, dissolved chemicals, workers, or any transferable thing.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都保留同一个意象：从一处连到另一处的一条虚线。变化的只是沿这条线走的是什么——定居者、鸟、整批人口、记录、细胞、溶解的化学物质、工人，或任何可转移之物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: at dusk a wedge of birds leaves one marsh for another.
core.cn: 核心意象：暮色中一群鸟排成人字，离开一片湿地飞向另一片。

branches.en: PEOPLE MOVING: settlers change home, and workers change region in search of wages.
branches.cn: 人的移动：定居者换了家，工人为工资换了地区。

branches.en: ANIMALS MOVING: the same route is flown or walked each season, often back and forth.
branches.cn: 动物的移动：同一路线每个季节被飞过或走过，常常来回。

branches.en: THE WAVE: many journeys counted together become a demographic or ecological trend.
branches.cn: 浪潮：许多趟行程合并计数，就成为人口或生态趋势。

branches.en: INVISIBLE MOVERS: records leave one system, cells leave one position, both by the same literal image.
branches.cn: 看不见的移动者：记录离开一套系统，细胞离开一个位置，两者用的是同一个字面意象。

branches.en: SUBSTANCES AND TRANSFERS: pollutants travel through soil and water, and any item can be moved between containers.
branches.cn: 物质与转移：污染物穿过土壤与水，任何东西都可以从一个容器搬到另一个。

intro.en: Migration is Latin migr- plus -ation. The ending -ation names an action; the stem migr- comes from migrare 'to move from one place to another', and the prefixes e- and im- decide the direction of the move.
intro.cn: migration 是拉丁词干 migr- 加 -ation。词尾 -ation 命名动作；词干 migr- 来自 migrare「从一处移到另一处」，而前缀 e- 与 im- 决定移动的方向。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb is migrare 'to move, change place'. Its family splits by prefix: e- 'out' gives emigrate, im- 'in' gives immigrate, and trans- 'across' gives transmigrate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁动词是 migrare「移动、换地方」。其词族按前缀分流：e-「向外」给出 emigrate，im-「向内」给出 immigrate，trans-「穿过」给出 transmigrate。

items.meaning: the act of moving from one place to another
items.meaningCN: 迁移；迁徙（-ation 构成动作名词）

items.meaning: to move from one region or system to another
items.example: Many birds migrate along this coast.
items.exampleCN: 许多鸟沿着这条海岸迁徙。

items.meaning: a person or animal that migrates
items.exampleCN: 这个营地安置着外来务工人员。

items.meaning: given to migrating, or relating to migration
to leave one's country to settle elsewhere
items.meaningCN: 移出本国；迁往外地（e- 表示向外）
items.exampleCN: 她家在 1980 年代移居国外。

items.meaning: the act of leaving a country
items.example: Emigration drained the island of young workers.
items.exampleCN: 人口外迁让这座岛失去了年轻劳力。

items.meaning: to come into a country to settle
items.meaningCN: 移入；移民入境（im- 表示向内）
items.exampleCN: 他们带着三个孩子移居入境。

items.meaning: the act of entering a country to settle
a passage across, or the passing of a soul into another body
items.meaningCN: 横越迁移；灵魂转世（trans- 表示穿过）
items.example: The old doctrine taught the transmigration of souls.
items.exampleCN: 这一古老教义讲灵魂的转世。

items.structure: the same adjective used in medicine for pain that moves
items.meaning: of symptoms that shift from one part to another
items.meaningCN: （医学）游走性的：症状从一处移到另一处
items.example: The patient reported migratory joint pain.
items.exampleCN: 病人诉称有关节游走性疼痛。

latinEntries.meaning: forms a noun of action or result
latinEntries.meaningCN: 构成表示动作或结果的名词

definition_zh: 苦行的；禁欲的；清心寡欲的；苦行者
definition_en: practicing strict self-denial and simple living, or a person who does so
core_image: 山洞里的苦行者：一张草席、一件粗衣、拒绝一切享乐
scene: 他放弃高薪工作，搬进山中木屋，每天只吃一餐、睡四小时。 The monk lived an ascetic life of prayer, fasting, and silence.
sceneCN: 这里 ascetic 是「苦行的、禁欲的」（第 1 个义项：自我克制的生活方式）；句意是僧侣过着祈祷、斋戒与静默的苦修生活。

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「苦行；禁欲主义」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「苦行地；清苦地」
希腊语同源词，义为「训练；修习」

senses.title: Self-denying in lifestyle
senses.definition: living simply and strictly, avoiding pleasures and comforts
senses.definitionCN: 生活简朴严格，回避享乐与舒适
senses.example: He kept an ascetic diet of rice, vegetables, and water.
senses.exampleCN: 他坚持米饭、蔬菜和清水的苦行饮食。
senses.why: Greek askesis meant training; just as athletes train hard, ascetics train the soul by refusing comfort.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 askesis 意为训练；正如运动员苦练，苦行者以拒绝舒适来锻炼灵魂。

senses.title: Severe and bare in style
senses.definition: plain and severe in appearance or atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 外表或氛围上朴素、严苛、毫无装饰
senses.example: The room had an ascetic beauty: white walls, a bare table, one chair.
senses.exampleCN: 房间有一种清苦之美：白墙、空桌、一把椅子。
senses.why: Denying comfort extends to design, where nothing decorative survives.
senses.whyCN: 对舒适的克制延伸到设计上，任何装饰都无法留存。

senses.title: A person practicing self-denial
senses.definition: one who renounces material comforts for spiritual discipline
senses.definitionCN: 为精神修习而放弃物质享受的人
senses.example: Desert ascetics were visited by pilgrims seeking wisdom.
senses.exampleCN: 朝圣者纷纷拜访沙漠中的苦行者，寻求智慧。
senses.why: When the adjective names a way of life, it also names the people who live it.
senses.whyCN: 当形容词指一种生活方式时，也指践行这种生活的人。

intro.en: Ascetic comes from Greek asketes, one who trains, from askein to exercise or train, first said of athletes.
intro.cn: ascetic 源自希腊语 askētēs（训练者），来自 askein（操练），最初形容运动员。

items.en: Askein meant to work raw material, then to train the body.
items.cn: 希腊语 askein 本指加工原料，后指训练身体。

items.en: Asketes named an athlete or one in training.
items.cn: askētēs 指运动员或受训者。

items.en: Christians applied the word to spiritual athletes, those training the soul.
items.cn: 希腊化时期基督徒把该词用于「灵魂的运动员」，即修行者。

items.en: Late Latin asceta meant a monk.
items.cn: 后期拉丁语 asceta 指僧侣。

items.en: English borrowed ascetic in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语借入 ascetic。

note.en: Ascetic describes chosen discipline, not poverty imposed from outside.
note.cn: ascetic 指主动选择的克己，而不是外界强加的贫困。

entries.definition: the doctrine or practice of self-denial
entries.definitionCN: 苦行主义；禁欲主义

entries.definition: relating to beauty, a different root entirely
entries.definitionCN: 审美的；美学的（拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: in an ascetic manner
entries.definitionCN: 苦行地；清苦地

entries.definition: Greek source word meaning one in training
entries.definitionCN: 希腊语源词，指受训者

entries.definition: of athletes, the original comparison for ascetics
entries.definitionCN: 运动的；运动员的（与苦行者本义相对照）

entries.definition: severe and plain, without comfort or luxury
entries.definitionCN: 严峻朴素的；清苦的

entries.definition: refusing one's own pleasures
entries.definitionCN: 克己的；自我否定的

entries.definition: like the life of a monastery
entries.definitionCN: 僧侣的；修道院式的

entries.definition: sparing and economical
entries.definitionCN: 节俭的

entries.definition: enduring hardship without complaint
entries.definitionCN: 坚忍的；禁欲的

normalIntro.en: Hear ask- inside ascetic: an ascetic asks nothing of comfort.
normalIntro.cn: 在 ascetic 里听出 ask（求）：苦行者对享乐「一无所求」。

normal.en: Greek askein: to train like an athlete.
normal.cn: 希腊语 askein：像运动员一样训练。

normal.en: ascetics are spiritual athletes.
normal.cn: 苦行者是「灵魂的运动员」。

normal.en: do not mix with aesthetic, about beauty.
normal.cn: 勿与 aesthetic（审美的）混淆。

normal.en: asceticism names the whole practice.
normal.cn: asceticism 指整套苦修实践。

normal.en: austerities are the deeds of an ascetic.
normal.cn: austerities 是苦行者的具体行为。

abstract.en: Picture a stone cell with one small window.
abstract.cn: 想象一间只有一个窄窗的石屋。

abstract.en: Feel the cold morning water of a ritual wash.
abstract.cn: 感受清晨仪式用水的冰冷。

abstract.en: See the athlete at dawn, training the soul instead of the body.
abstract.cn: 看见黎明训练的运动员——练的是灵魂而非身体。

examples.en: The founder lived an ascetic life until his death.
examples.cn: 创始人一生过着苦行的生活。

examples.en: Her ascetic apartment held only a mattress and books.
examples.cn: 她清苦的公寓里只有一张床垫和书。

examples.en: Ancient ascetics withdrew to the desert to pray.
examples.cn: 古代苦行者隐居沙漠祈祷。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「饿塞体」——饿着肚子、塞住欲望、修成身体之苦，正如 ascetic 的禁欲修行。

root: 源自希腊语 askein（操练、修习）与 askētēs（训练者），本用于运动员，后被基督教用于修行者。

sensesIntro.en: The athlete's training image moves from bodily discipline to spiritual denial to bare aesthetics.
sensesIntro.cn: 运动员训练的意象从身体的自律移向灵魂的克己，再到朴素无饰的风格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an athlete of the soul training by refusing comfort
core.cn: 核心意象：以拒绝舒适来训练的灵魂运动员

branches.en: strict self-denial in daily life
branches.cn: 日常生活中的严格克己

branches.en: bare, undecorated severity
branches.cn: 朴素无饰的严峻

branches.en: the person who renounces comfort
branches.cn: 放弃舒适的修行者

branches.en: discipline chosen for spirit
branches.cn: 为精神而选择的自律

branches.en: the visible mark of renunciation
branches.cn: 克己的外在印记

intro.en: The Greek askein family is small in English but carries the key idea of disciplined practice.
intro.cn: 希腊语 askein 词族在英语中虽小，却承载「修习」这一关键概念。

latinIntro.en: This is a Greek, not Latin, family; there are no Latin cognates in English.
latinIntro.cn: 这是希腊语词族而非拉丁语词族，英语中没有拉丁同源词。

items.meaning: one who lives in the wilderness

definition_zh: 达到；取得；抵达；成就；学识；造诣；学业成绩；达标指标
definition_en: the act of reaching or obtaining something through effort, and the achievement or level that results from it
core_image: 攀岩者的指尖终于触到岩壁顶端那条边——达到，就是努力伸长之后终于碰到目标的那一下
scene: 教育大臣举起一张图表，说我们只量得出成绩，却量不出孩子的好奇心。 An education minister holds up a chart and says: We measure attainment, but a child's curiosity never appears on the chart.
sceneCN: 这里 attainment 先用「学业成绩、达到水平」（第 7 个义项：教育测量中的达到程度），再暗含「成就、素养」；句意：我们测量学业成绩，但孩子的好奇心从不出现在图表上。画面里有折线图、成绩单和一支教鞭。

pos.zh: 达到；取得；成就；学识；学业成绩

derivatives.zh: 无法达到的；高不可攀的

senses.title: The act of reaching
senses.titleCN: 达到：把努力伸到目标上
senses.definition: the act of reaching something that has been the object of effort
senses.definitionCN: 经过努力而触及某个目标的行为
senses.example: The attainment of fluency in a second language takes years of daily practice.
senses.exampleCN: 第二语言流利程度的达到需要多年每日练习。
senses.why: -ment names the act, as in movement and payment; attain goes back to ad- 'to' + tangere 'touch'. The act is imagined as contact: you do not merely want the goal, you stretch until you touch it.
senses.whyCN: -ment 像 movement、payment 一样把动词变成「行为」；attain 出自 ad-「向」+ tangere「触碰」。这个行为被想象成一次接触：不是只想要目标，而是一直伸到碰着它。

senses.title: Arriving at a place
senses.definition: the act of arriving at a place or at the end of a journey
senses.definitionCN: 到达某地或走完一段旅程的行为
senses.example: The attainment of the summit came after nine hours of climbing.
senses.exampleCN: 在攀登九个小时之后，他们抵达了顶峰。
senses.why: Latin attingere meant both 'to touch' and 'to arrive at': a ship touches shore, a climber touches rock. English kept the literal spatial sense beside the figurative one.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 attingere 既指「触碰」，也指「到达」：船靠岸是 touch，登山者碰着岩壁也是 touch。英语把字面的空间义和比喻义一并保留下来。

senses.title: Making a goal real
senses.definition: the successful bringing about of a goal, standard, or agreement
senses.definitionCN: 目标、标准或协议的顺利实现
senses.example: The attainment of the treaty took two years of quiet diplomacy.
senses.exampleCN: 这份条约的达成用了两年安静的外交斡旋。
senses.why: The object of attaining can be abstract; a standard or an agreement is 'reached' once its conditions are met. The spatial metaphor is extended to anything with a threshold.
senses.whyCN: attain 的宾语可以是抽象物；标准或协议的条件一满足，就算「够到了」。这个空间比喻被推广到一切有门槛的事物。

senses.title: Obtaining a right or status
senses.definition: the obtaining of a right, qualification, or status, especially in formal use
senses.definitionCN: 权利、资格或身份的获得，尤用于正式语境
senses.example: Attainment of citizenship requires five years of residence.
senses.exampleCN: 取得公民身份需要居住满五年。
senses.why: Official English uses attainment for entering a status: citizenship, majority, a qualification. The status is treated as a place, and its conditions are the road that leads there.
senses.whyCN: 正式英语用 attainment 表示进入某种身份：公民资格、成年、资历。身份被当成一个地点，条件则是通往那里的路。

senses.title: A thing achieved
senses.titleCN: 成就：够下来的那件东西
senses.definition: an achievement or accomplishment, especially one won by sustained effort
senses.definitionCN: 尤指靠持续努力赢得的成就或业绩
senses.example: His greatest attainment was the bridge that still carries traffic today.
senses.exampleCN: 他最大的成就是那座至今仍在通车的桥。
senses.why: From the 1670s the noun also named the thing at the end of effort, not the effort itself. Since -ment can denote a result (as in 'a payment'), the touch became a possession.
senses.whyCN: 从 17 世纪 70 年代起，这个名词也指努力尽头的那件东西，而不只是努力本身。-ment 能表示结果（如 a payment），于是那一下触碰变成了一份所有物。

senses.title: Learned skill, usually plural
senses.titleCN: 学识：已经收进身体里的东西
senses.definition: a level of knowledge or skill in a subject, especially when impressive or scholarly
senses.definitionCN: 某一学科的知识或技能水平，尤指令人印象深刻或具学术性的
senses.example: She is a scholar of great attainments in medieval history.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一位在中世纪史方面造诣很深的学者。
senses.why: The plural shifted the image from the act to the height reached: knowledge is what remains after the climb. The usage is slightly formal and old-fashioned, suited to praising a scholar.
senses.whyCN: 复数把意象从「动作」转到「达到的高度」：知识是攀登之后留在身上的东西。这种用法略正式、偏旧，适合称赞学者。

senses.title: Measured school level
senses.titleCN: 学业水平：把高度画成刻度
senses.definition: a pupil's measured level of knowledge, as recorded in school assessments
senses.definitionCN: 学生在学校评估中记录的知识水平
senses.example: Boys in the sample showed lower attainment in reading than girls.
senses.exampleCN: 样本中的男孩在阅读上表现出的学业水平低于女孩。
senses.why: Twentieth-century education made the height measurable: attainment became a score along a scale, used to compare groups. A metaphor of distance turned into a statistic.
senses.whyCN: 20 世纪的教育把这个高度变成可测量的东西：attainment 成了刻度上的分数，用来比较群体。距离的比喻由此变成统计数字。

senses.title: Attainment target
senses.titleCN: 达标指标：必须碰到的那条线
senses.definition: an official target set for pupils' or schools' results, used especially in British education
senses.definitionCN: 为学生或学校成绩设定的官方指标，尤用于英国教育
senses.example: The school narrowly missed its attainment target in mathematics.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校以微弱差距未达到数学科的达标指标。
senses.why: British policy fixed 'attainment target' as an administrative phrase: the level a pupil or school is required to touch. The old image survives intact inside a government document.
senses.whyCN: 英国政策把 attainment target 固定为行政用语：学生或学校必须碰到的那条线。旧的意象原封不动地活在一份政府文件里。

senses.title: Something obtained
senses.titleCN: 取得物：努力留下的结果
senses.definition: something that has been obtained or brought into being as a result of effort
senses.definitionCN: 经努力而获得或产生的某物
senses.example: Clean water is an attainment that many villages still lack.
senses.exampleCN: 清洁的水是许多村庄至今仍未取得的一样东西。
senses.why: The result sense generalizes: anything brought into being by effort can be called an attainment, even an abstract good. Effort leaves a trace, and the trace takes the name of the act.
senses.whyCN: 结果义进一步推广：任何靠努力产生的东西都能叫 attainment，哪怕是抽象的好事。努力留下痕迹，而这道痕迹沿用了动作的名字。

intro.en: Attainment is the noun of an old verb of touching. Latin tangere 'to touch' became attingere 'to reach by touching', French ataindre 'to reach', and English attain; the suffix -ment then turns the reaching into something nameable, countable and gradable.
intro.cn: attainment 是一个古老「触碰」动词的名词形式。拉丁语 tangere「触碰」变成 attingere「触而及之」，再变成法语 ataindre「达到」和英语 attain；后缀 -ment 又把「够到」变成可以命名、计数、评级的东西。

items.en: The root *tag- 'to touch, handle' is reconstructed from Latin tangere and its cognates. There is no written record of this layer, so it is marked source uncertain.
items.cn: 词根 *tag-「触碰、摆弄」是从拉丁语 tangere 及其同源词重构出来的。这一层没有书面记录，因此标为「来源不确定」。

items.en: Tangere 'to touch' formed attingere 'to touch; arrive at', from ad- 'to' + tangere. Latin already used the compound for 'attack, strike, manage', all felt as kinds of contact.
items.cn: tangere「触碰」构成 attingere「触及；到达」，由 ad-「向」+ tangere 组成。拉丁语已用它表示「攻击、打击、处理」，这些都被感受为不同方式的接触。

items.en: ataindre 'to come up to, reach, attain, strive' (Modern French atteindre) came from Vulgar Latin *attangere and supplied the stem ataign- that English borrowed.
items.cn: 古法语 ataindre「走近、达到、努力争取」（现代法语 atteindre）出自通俗拉丁语 *attangere，并提供了英语借入的词干 ataign-。

items.en: attain is recorded as 'succeed in reaching, come so near as to touch'. The borrowing belongs to the years around 1300, the period often described as the early 14th century.
items.cn: attain 被记录为「成功到达、近到可以触碰」。这一借入发生在 1300 年前后，也就是通常所说的 14 世纪初。

items.en: attainment enters through French atteignement as 'the action of acquiring by effort'. The suffix -ment names the act, as it does in payment and movement.
items.cn: attainment 经法语 atteignement 进入英语，意为「靠努力获取的行为」。后缀 -ment 命名动作，和 payment、movement 一样。

items.en: 'That which is attained, a personal accomplishment' is recorded from the 1670s. The plural attainments came to mean learned skill, and educational attainment and attainment target are 20th-century measurements.
items.cn: 「所达到之物、个人成就」记录于 17 世纪 70 年代。复数 attainments 后来指学术造诣，而 educational attainment 与 attainment target 是 20 世纪的测量用语。

note.en: The first group shares the -tainment ending or the tain/tang- root; the second group names results of effort that attainment can also denote.
note.cn: 第一组共享 -tainment 词尾或 tain/tang- 词根；第二组是 attainment 也能指称的各种努力成果。

entries.definition: to reach or obtain something by effort. It is the base of attainment, with the same tain/tang- root.
entries.definitionCN: 达到；获得。它是 attainment 的基础词，共享 tain/tang- 词根。

entries.definition: able to be reached or achieved. The -able suffix says the goal can be touched.
entries.definitionCN: 可达到的；可实现的。-able 后缀表示目标能够被够到。

entries.definition: the act of making amends, literally 'at-one-ment', from at + one. It is not related to attain.
entries.definitionCN: 赎罪；弥补，字面是 at-one-ment「成为一体」，由 at + one 构成，与 attain 不同源。

entries.definition: a reduction or lessening, from Old French abatre 'to beat down'. Only the -ment ending resembles attainment.
entries.definitionCN: 减轻；减少，出自古法语 abatre「打倒」。只有 -ment 词尾与 attainment 相似。

entries.definition: a thing accomplished by effort, especially something notable. It matches the 'thing achieved' sense of attainment.
entries.definitionCN: 成就；业绩。对应 attainment 的「成就」义。

entries.definition: the successful completion of a task, or a skill so gained. It stresses the finishing rather than the reaching.
entries.definitionCN: 完成；成就；才艺。它强调「完成」而非「够到」。

entries.definition: the act of obtaining something, especially knowledge or property. It fits the 'obtaining' sense of attainment.
entries.definitionCN: 获得；取得，尤指知识或财产。对应 attainment 的「取得」义。

entries.definition: the achievement of a desire, promise, or potential. It adds a sense of completeness to attainment.
entries.definitionCN: 实现；满足。它在 attainment 之上加了「圆满」的意味。

entries.definition: to arrive at or attain, or the distance one can stretch. It is the everyday word behind attainment's formal noun.
entries.definitionCN: 到达；够到；可及的距离。它是 attainment 这个正式名词背后的日常词。

normalIntro.en: The family is about contact: attain, contact, tangible and contagion all descend from Latin tangere 'to touch'.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词族讲的是「接触」：attain、contact、tangible、contagion 都出自拉丁语 tangere「触碰」。

normal.en: at- 'to' + tain 'touch' + -ment: attainment is effort ending in contact.
normal.cn: at-「向」+ tain「触碰」+ -ment：attainment 就是努力以「碰上」收尾。

normal.en: Think of a target: an attainment target is the line a pupil must touch.
normal.cn: 想想靶子：attainment target 就是学生必须碰到的那条线。

normal.en: attain, contact and tangible all hide tangere, 'to touch'.
normal.cn: attain、contact、tangible 都藏着 tangere「触碰」。

normal.en: A person's attainments are the things already touched and kept — knowledge included.
normal.cn: 一个人的 attainments 是已经碰到并留下来的东西——包括知识。

normal.en: At the finish line the runner's hand touches the tape: that touch is the attainment.
normal.cn: 终点线上，跑者的手碰到绶带：那一下触碰就是 attainment。

abstract.en: The word always keeps a body in it: reaching is not wishing, it is extending until contact.
abstract.cn: 这个词里始终有一个身体：达到不是许愿，而是一直伸展到接触为止。

abstract.en: Act and result share one suffix: what you do and what you get are both -ment.
abstract.cn: 动作与结果共用一个后缀：你做的和你得的都是 -ment。

abstract.en: A school report measures a touch: how far a hand has stretched along a scale.
abstract.cn: 一份成绩单测量的是一次触碰：一只手沿刻度伸出了多远。

examples.en: The attainment of independence took decades of negotiation.
examples.cn: 独立的取得用了数十年的谈判。

examples.en: Her attainments in chemistry won her a place in the academy.
examples.cn: 她在化学上的造诣为她赢得了科学院的一席之地。

examples.en: The attainment gap between rich and poor pupils has widened.
examples.cn: 贫富学生之间的学业成绩差距扩大了。

dict_mnemonic.text: at（啊）+ tain（抬）+ ment（门）——啊，把东西抬到门楣上，终于够着了 → attainment 达到；成就

root: 源自拉丁语 attingere（ad-「向」+ tangere「触碰」）「触及、到达」，经古法语 ataindre 进入英语；核心是「努力伸长直到碰到目标」，再加 -ment 把这一动作及其结果名词化。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one gesture: reaching out until the fingers touch the goal. What is touched becomes an arrival, a right, an achievement, a body of learning, and finally a line on a school report.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟着同一个动作走：把手伸出去，直到指尖碰到目标。被碰到的可以是抵达、一项权利、一件成就、一身学问，最后变成成绩单上的一条线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the hand stretching out and finally touching the goal.
core.cn: 核心意象：手一直伸出去，终于触到目标。

branches.en: THE ACT OF REACHING: effort making contact with a goal, whether a place, a standard or an agreement.
branches.cn: 达到的动作：努力与目标接触，无论目标是地点、标准还是协议。

branches.en: ARRIVAL: the literal touch of a shore, a summit or a finish line.
branches.cn: 抵达：字面地碰到海岸、山顶或终点线。

branches.en: OBTAINING: a right or status entered, and any thing left behind by effort.
branches.cn: 取得：进入某种权利或身份，以及努力留下的任何东西。

branches.en: WHAT IS WON: a single achievement, and the accumulated learning a person carries.
branches.cn: 所获：一件成就，以及一个人身上积累的学问。

branches.en: MEASURED HEIGHT: a score on a school scale and the official target line.
branches.cn: 被测出的高度：学校刻度上的分数，以及官方设定的目标线。

intro.en: attainment is at- (ad-, 'to') + tain (tang-, 'touch') + -ment (act or result noun). The same tang- root, worn down to -tain or -tact, runs through contact, contagion, tangible and tactile.
intro.cn: attainment 是 at-（ad-「向」）+ tain（tang-「触碰」）+ -ment（行为或结果名词）。同一个 tang- 词根磨成 -tain 或 -tact 后，贯穿 contact、contagion、tangible、tactile。

latinIntro.en: Latin tangere 'to touch' yields attingere 'reach', contingere 'touch together' (whence contact), and tangibilis 'touchable'; its past participle tactus gives tactile.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tangere「触碰」给出 attingere「达到」、contingere「共同触及」（即 contact 的来源）和 tangibilis「可触的」；其过去分词 tactus 给出 tactile。

items.structure: at- (ad-, to) + tain (tang-, touch) + -ment (noun of act/result)
items.meaning: the act of reaching; an achievement or measured level
items.example: The attainment of a degree opened the door to research.
items.exampleCN: 取得学位为研究工作打开了大门。

items.meaning: to reach or achieve something by effort
items.example: Few runners attain that pace without years of training.
items.exampleCN: 没有多年训练，很少有跑者能达到那种配速。

items.example: Set an attainable goal for the first month.
items.exampleCN: 为第一个月设定一个可实现的目标。

items.meaningCN: 无法达到的；高不可攀的
items.example: Perfect fairness is an unattainable ideal.
items.exampleCN: 完全公平是一种无法达到的理想。

items.example: The report questions the attainability of the targets.
items.exampleCN: 报告质疑这些目标的可实现性。

items.meaning: the state of touching or communicating
items.example: The two plates meet at a point of contact.
items.exampleCN: 两块板在一个接触点相接。

items.meaning: the spreading of disease by contact
items.example: Doctors once blamed contagion on bad air.
items.exampleCN: 医生们曾把接触传染归咎于污浊的空气。

items.meaning: able to be passed on by contact
able to be touched, hence real and concrete
items.exampleCN: 这个项目产生了实实在在的成果。

items.meaning: not able to be touched; abstract

latinEntries.meaning: to touch; to handle; to reach
to touch; to arrive at; to attain

definition_zh: v. 攀登；上升；登上（王位等）；（道路）向上倾斜
definition_en: To go up or climb towards a higher point; to rise to a higher rank or position; of a path, to slope upwards.
core_image: 脚一级一级往上踩，位置越来越高
scene: 缆车沿着陡坡缓缓爬升。 The cable car began to ascend the steep slope.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：ascend 指往高处移动、攀登，比 climb 更正式。

senses.title: To go up towards a higher point
senses.definition: to climb or move upwards, a more formal word than climb
senses.definitionCN: 向上攀登或移动，比 climb 更正式
senses.example: We ascended the ridge before sunrise.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在日出前登上了山脊。
senses.why: The root means to climb, and the prefix means to, so the word paints movement directed at a height.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为「爬」，前缀意为「向」，所以这个词画的是朝着某个高处的移动。

senses.title: To rise to a higher position
senses.definition: to reach a higher rank, office or throne, without any physical climbing
senses.definitionCN: 取得更高的等级、职位或王位，不涉及身体的攀爬
senses.example: She ascended the throne at the age of twenty.
senses.exampleCN: 她二十岁登上王位。
senses.why: Height is the oldest metaphor for rank, so the climbing verb was borrowed for thrones and offices.
senses.whyCN: 「高」是最古老的地位隐喻，于是这个表示攀爬的动词被借去说王位与职位。

senses.title: To slope upwards
senses.definition: of a road, path or ground, to rise as it goes forward
senses.definitionCN: 指道路、小径或地面向前延伸时逐渐升高
senses.example: The track ascends sharply after the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 过了桥之后小路陡然上行。
senses.why: Here nothing moves at all: the shape of the ground itself is described as if it were climbing.
senses.whyCN: 这里其实什么都没动：地面的形状本身被描述成好像在往上爬。

intro.en: Ascend is Latin ascendere, from ad, to, plus scandere, to climb; the same climbing root gives descend, scale and scandal.
intro.cn: ascend 就是拉丁语 ascendere，由 ad「向」加 scandere「爬」构成；同一「爬」词根还给出 descend、scale 与 scandal。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning to jump or climb lies behind several words for going up and for stumbling.
items.cn: 一个拟构的印欧词根意为「跳、爬」，藏在若干表示上升与绊倒的词背后。

items.en: Latin scandere meant to climb, and also to scan verse by counting its steps.
items.cn: 拉丁语 scandere 意为「攀登」，也指按音步「划分诗句」。

items.en: With ad, to, the verb ascendere meant to climb up towards something.
items.cn: 加上 ad「向」之后，动词 ascendere 意为「朝某处往上爬」。

items.en: Old French kept the verb and passed it on with the sense of rising in rank as well as in space.
items.cn: 古法语保留了这个动词，并同时传递「地位上升」与「空间上升」两层意思。

items.en: English records ascend from the fourteenth century, at first mainly of climbing and of heavenly rising.
items.cn: 英语从十四世纪起记录 ascend，起初主要用于攀登与升天。

items.en: By the fifteenth century the verb was standard for reaching a throne or an office.
items.cn: 到十五世纪，这个动词已成为「登上王位或职位」的标准说法。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the climbing root and adds two words that only share the opening sound; the near-meaning group grades ways of going up.
note.cn: 形近组保留「爬」词根，并加上两个只是开头音相同的词；近义组按方式区分各种「往上」。

entries.definition: To go down from a higher place.
entries.definitionCN: 从高处往下走。

entries.definition: The act of going up, or an upward slope.
entries.definitionCN: 上升的动作，或向上的坡。

entries.definition: Severely self-disciplined, avoiding comfort.
entries.definitionCN: 严苦自律、不享安逸的。

entries.definition: To find out something for certain.
entries.definitionCN: 把某事查明弄清。

entries.definition: To go up using hands, feet or effort.
entries.definitionCN: 用手脚或力气往上。

entries.definition: To move to a higher level or amount.
entries.definitionCN: 升到更高的位置或数量。

entries.definition: To go up, or to get onto something.
entries.definitionCN: 往上走，或登上某物。

entries.definition: To climb something high and difficult.
entries.definitionCN: 攀上又高又难的东西。

normalIntro.en: Ascend is ad, to, plus scandere, climb: climbing towards something, whether a ridge or a throne.
normalIntro.cn: ascend 就是 ad「向」加 scandere「爬」：朝着某处往上爬，那处可以是山脊，也可以是王位。

normal.en: Descend is the same root turned downwards.
normal.cn: descend 是同一词根朝下的方向。

normal.en: Ascent is the noun, ascension the formal noun.
normal.cn: ascent 是名词，ascension 是更正式的名词。

normal.en: Ascend the throne needs no preposition.
normal.cn: ascend the throne 不需要介词。

normal.en: Ascend to power does need to.
normal.cn: ascend to power 则需要 to。

normal.en: Ascending order means from small to large.
normal.cn: ascending order 意为从小到大。

abstract.en: Picture feet finding one step after another.
abstract.cn: 想象双脚一级一级找到台阶。

abstract.en: Imagine a crown settling on a young head.
abstract.cn: 想象一顶王冠落在年轻的头上。

abstract.en: Think of a path that keeps tilting upward.
abstract.cn: 想象一条不断向上翘起的小路。

examples.en: The balloon ascended above the clouds.
examples.cn: 气球升到云层之上。

examples.en: He ascended to the directorship last spring.
examples.cn: 他去年春天升任主管。

examples.en: Sort the numbers in ascending order.
examples.cn: 把数字按升序排列。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：a-「向」+ scend「爬」——朝着高处爬，就是 ascend；换成 de-「向下」便成 descend。

root: 拉丁语 scandere「爬」加 ad-「向」构成 ascendere「向上攀」，经古法语入十四世纪英语；同根还有 descend「下降」、ascent「上升」与 scan「按音步划分」。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses are one upward line: a body climbing, a name rising in rank, and ground that tilts as it runs forward.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项是同一条向上的线：身体在攀、名位在升、地面向前延伸时向上翘。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: feet finding one step after another, ever higher
core.cn: 核心意象：脚一级一级往上踩，位置越来越高

branches.en: A ridge reached before sunrise.
branches.cn: 日出前登上的山脊。

branches.en: A balloon above the clouds.
branches.cn: 升到云层之上的气球。

branches.en: A crown settling on a young head.
branches.cn: 落在年轻头上的王冠。

branches.en: A track tilting up after the bridge.
branches.cn: 过桥后向上翘的小路。

branches.en: One upward line in space, rank and shape.
branches.cn: 空间、地位与形状中的同一条上行线。

intro.en: Ascend is a- from ad- plus -scend, climb; the same root builds descend, transcend, ascent and scan.
intro.cn: ascend 由 ad- 变来的 a- 加 -scend「爬」构成；同一词根还构成 descend、transcend、ascent 与 scan。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is scandere, to climb, ascendere, to climb up, and ascensus, a climbing; scala, a ladder, gives scale beside it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 scandere「爬」、ascendere「向上攀」与 ascensus「攀登」；旁边的 scala「梯子」产生 scale。

definition_zh: 可持续发展；既满足当代需要又不损害后代满足其需要能力的发展
definition_en: development that meets present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet theirs
core_image: 一座城市在生长，同时老树林与河岸被原样保留，新旧并排
scene: 新建的街区旁边保留着老树林与河岸，工地与绿地在同一张图上并存。 The city adopted a sustainable development plan for the riverfront.
sceneCN: 这里 sustainable development 指「兼顾当代与后代需求的发展方式」（第 1 个义项：既满足当前需要，又不削弱后代满足其需要的能力）；句意为这座城市为滨河地区通过了可持续发展规划。图中可辨识物件：新楼、保留的老树、河岸步道、铺开的规划图。

pos.zh: 可持续发展（不可数固定短语）

collocations.zh: 为可持续发展提供资金

senses.title: Meeting present needs without harming the future
senses.titleCN: 满足当代而不损害后代
senses.definition: development that satisfies current needs while leaving later generations the same ability to satisfy theirs
senses.definitionCN: 在满足当前需要的同时，让后代保有同样的满足其需要的能力
senses.example: The city adopted a sustainable development plan for the riverfront.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市为滨河地区通过了可持续发展规划。
senses.why: sustainable says the process can be kept up, and development says it grows; together they demand growth that does not consume its own support.
senses.whyCN: sustainable 表示过程能维持下去，development 表示它在生长；两者合起来要求增长不消耗自身的支撑条件。

senses.title: A policy framework and its goals
senses.definition: the international framework of goals, targets and reports built around that principle
senses.definitionCN: 围绕这一原则建立的国际目标、指标与报告体系
senses.example: The country reported progress against the sustainable development goals.
senses.exampleCN: 该国报告了在可持续发展目标上的进展。
senses.why: a principle becomes a policy when it is written into goals with numbers and deadlines.
senses.whyCN: 当原则被写成带数字与期限的目标，它就成为政策。

senses.title: Managing resources so they renew
senses.titleCN: 以可再生方式管理资源
senses.definition: the practice of using soil, water, forests and fish no faster than they can renew
senses.definitionCN: 使用土壤、水、森林与鱼类时不超过其再生速度的做法
senses.example: Forestry schools teach sustainable development through rotation cycles.
senses.exampleCN: 林业学校通过轮伐周期讲授可持续发展。
senses.why: the oldest use of sustainable is about keeping a yield going, so resource management is its natural home.
senses.whyCN: sustainable 最古老的用法就是让产量延续，因此资源管理是它最自然的归属。

senses.title: Growth decoupled from damage
senses.titleCN: 与损害脱钩的增长模式
senses.definition: an economic model in which output rises while resource use and pollution fall
senses.definitionCN: 产出上升而资源使用与污染下降的经济模式
senses.example: The report measured sustainable development as growth per tonne of carbon.
senses.exampleCN: 报告用每吨碳对应的增长来衡量可持续发展。
senses.why: economists keep development as growth but attach a condition: the growth must not raise its material cost.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家保留 development 的增长含义，但附加条件：增长不得抬高其物质代价。

senses.title: A planning principle for places
senses.definition: a rule for designing towns and regions so that transport, housing and green space last
senses.definitionCN: 设计城镇与区域时使交通、住房与绿地都能持久运作的规则
senses.example: The riverfront plan applies sustainable development block by block.
senses.exampleCN: 滨河规划逐街区地应用可持续发展原则。
senses.why: planners turn the principle into setbacks, density limits and preserved corridors.
senses.whyCN: 规划者把原则变成退线、密度上限与保留廊道。

senses.title: A corporate strategy label
senses.definition: the label companies use for environmental and social targets in their reporting
senses.definitionCN: 公司在报告中用于环境与社会目标的标签
senses.example: The firm folded sustainable development into its annual report.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司把可持续发展并入年度报告。
senses.why: when investors ask for non-financial performance, the phrase becomes a heading in corporate disclosure.
senses.whyCN: 当投资者要求非财务绩效，这个短语就成了企业披露中的一个标题。

senses.title: Any practice that keeps a system going
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：使系统得以延续的做法
senses.definition: any arrangement that lets a system continue without exhausting what supports it
senses.definitionCN: 任何使系统在不耗尽支撑条件的情况下继续运转的安排
senses.example: The coach called rotation sustainable development for the squad.
senses.exampleCN: 教练把轮换称作球队的可持续发展。
senses.why: the phrase keeps only its logical shape, so it can describe a team, a diet or a budget.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语只保留其逻辑形态，因此可描述球队、饮食或预算。

senses.title: A slogan open to greenwashing
senses.definition: the phrase used as a slogan whose record may not match its promise
senses.definitionCN: 被当作标语使用、实际记录却可能与承诺不符的说法
senses.example: Critics called the advertisement sustainable development in name only.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者称这则广告只是名义上的可持续发展。
senses.why: a phrase broad enough to sell anything invites the charge that it means nothing.
senses.whyCN: 一个宽到可以推销任何东西的短语，难免被指为空话。

intro.en: Sustainable development joins Latin sustinere 'to hold up' with Old French desveloper 'to unwrap'. The fixed phrase became prominent through the 1987 Brundtland Report. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: sustainable development 把拉丁 sustinere「从下面托住」与古法语 desveloper「解开包裹」并置。这个固定短语经 1987 年布伦特兰报告而广为人知。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sub- 'up from below' plus tenere 'to hold' produced sustinere 'to hold up, maintain, endure'. The image is a hand under a weight.
items.cn: sub-「从下往上」加 tenere「握住」构成 sustinere「托住、维持、承受」。意象是一只手在重物下方支撑。

items.en: Old French sustenir carried the verb into English as sustain in the thirteenth century, first for holding up a thing or a claim.
items.cn: 古法语 sustenir 在 13 世纪把这个动词带入英语，成为 sustain，最初指托住物体或支撑主张。

items.en: Desveloper meant 'to unwrap, unfurl', from des- 'undo' plus a second element of uncertain origin, perhaps Germanic.
items.cn: desveloper 意为「解开、展开」，由 des-「去除」加一个来源不确定的成分构成，该成分可能来自日耳曼语。

items.en: English development first meant an unfolding or a gradual revelation, and only later the growth of towns, economies and capabilities.
items.cn: 英语 development 最初指展开或逐渐显现，后来才指城镇、经济与能力的增长。

items.en: The 1987 report Our Common Future fixed the modern definition, and the phrase then spread into treaties, curricula and corporate reports.
items.cn: 1987 年的《我们共同的未来》固定了现代定义，这个短语随后进入条约、课程与企业报告。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and second element): earlier isolated uses exist, the exact first appearance is not fixed, and the origin of the desveloper element is unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与第二成分）：更早的零星用例存在，确切首见时间没有定说，desveloper 第二成分的来源亦无定论。

note.en: Group one holds forms that share sustain or develop and are easily confused; group two holds neighbouring policy ideas with a different emphasis.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 sustain 或 develop、容易混淆的形式；第二组是侧重点不同的邻近政策概念。

entries.definition: The past participle meaning 'continued for a long time', as in sustained growth; it describes duration, not the ability to continue.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词，意为「持续了很长时间的」，如持续增长；它描述持续时间，不描述延续能力。

entries.definition: Able to be kept going over time; it is the first element of the phrase and can stand alone.
entries.definitionCN: 能够长期维持的；它是短语的第一个成分，也可单独使用。

entries.definition: From the same Latin verb: that which holds a person up, usually food or livelihood.
entries.definitionCN: 同出这一拉丁动词：支撑人的东西，通常指食物或生计。

entries.definition: The noun for growth or unfolding; on its own it carries no promise of restraint.
entries.definitionCN: 表示增长或展开的名词；单独使用时并不包含克制的承诺。

entries.definition: Growth that can continue without collapse; it stresses output rather than the needs of future generations.
entries.definitionCN: 能够不崩溃地持续的增长；它强调产出，而非后代的需求。

entries.definition: A policy label that stresses low pollution and low carbon, often without the full intergenerational definition.
entries.definitionCN: 强调低污染与低碳的政策标签，通常不含完整的代际定义。

entries.definition: A model that keeps materials in use by reuse and repair; it is one way to pursue sustainable development.
entries.definitionCN: 通过再利用与修复让材料持续使用的模式；它是实现可持续发展的一种方式。

entries.definition: Protecting nature as such; sustainable development also includes economic and social goals.
entries.definitionCN: 保护自然本身；可持续发展还包含经济与社会目标。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: sustinere 'hold up' + desveloper 'unwrap': keep the support under the growth.
normal.cn: sustinere「托住」+ desveloper「展开」：在增长下方一直托着支撑。

normal.en: The family runs sustain, sustainable, sustainability, sustainably, unsustainable.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 sustain、sustainable、sustainability、sustainably、unsustainable。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the policy sense: sustainable development goals, strategy, indicators.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出政策义：可持续发展目标、战略、指标。

normal.en: The Latin image is a hand under a weight: support, not speed.
normal.cn: 拉丁意象是一只手托着重物：讲的是支撑，不是速度。

normal.en: The 1987 Brundtland definition is the one quoted in treaties: present needs without harming future ability.
normal.cn: 条约常引的是 1987 年布伦特兰定义：满足当代而不损害后代的能力。

abstract.en: Picture a ladder that repairs its own rungs as you climb.
abstract.cn: 想象一架梯子，你往上爬时它自己修补横档。

abstract.en: Picture a budget that pays today's bills and leaves tomorrow's intact.
abstract.cn: 想象一份预算，付清今天的账，又不动明天的钱。

abstract.en: Picture a tree whose shade is used without cutting the trunk.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵树，人们用它的树荫，却不砍它的树干。

examples.en: The syllabus treats sustainable development as an economic issue too.
examples.cn: 这份教学大纲把可持续发展也当作经济问题。

examples.en: Fishing quotas are a test of sustainable development in practice.
examples.cn: 捕鱼配额是可持续发展在实践中的一次检验。

examples.en: The bank refused to fund the mine on sustainable development grounds.
examples.cn: 银行以可持续发展为由拒绝为这座矿提供资金。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「sustainable（能撑住的）+ development（发展）」——能一直撑下去的发展 → 可持续发展
