root: sustain 来自拉丁 sustinere「托住、维持」= sub-「从下」+ tenere「握住」；develop 经古法语 desveloper「解开包裹」，其第二成分来源不确定；development 的「发展」义为后起。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one condition: a process must keep its own support intact. That condition is then applied to international goals, resource management, growth models, town plans, corporate reports, any continuing system, and finally to the phrase used as an empty slogan.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个条件展开：过程必须保持自身支撑完好。这个条件随后用于国际目标、资源管理、增长模式、城镇规划、企业报告、任何延续中的系统，最后用于被当作空口号的短语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a growing town that keeps its old trees and riverbank standing beside the new blocks.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座生长的城镇，让老树与河岸立在新街区旁边。

branches.en: THE CORE CONDITION: present need is met, and future ability is left whole.
branches.cn: 核心条件：当代需要得到满足，后代能力保持完整。

branches.en: GOALS AND RENEWAL: the principle is written into targets and into harvest rates that let a stock renew.
branches.cn: 目标与再生：原则被写进指标，也写进让存量再生的采获速率。

branches.en: GROWTH AND REPORTING: economists decouple output from damage, and firms adopt the label for disclosure.
branches.cn: 增长与披露：经济学家让产出与损害脱钩，企业采用这一标签作披露。

branches.en: PLANNING: the rule becomes setbacks, density limits and preserved corridors.
branches.cn: 规划：规则变成退线、密度上限与保留廊道。

branches.en: GENERALIZED AND EMPTY: any system can be kept going, and any slogan can abuse the phrase.
branches.cn: 泛化与空化：任何系统都可维持，任何口号都可滥用这个短语。

intro.en: Sustainable development is a phrase of two learned nouns: an adjective built on a Latin verb and a noun built on a French verb. Both halves are still productive, so the phrase can be read piece by piece.
intro.cn: sustainable development 是两个学术名词构成的短语：一个由拉丁动词构成的形容词，加一个由法语动词构成的名词。两半都仍有构词能力，因此这个短语可以逐块读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin tenere 'to hold' gives sustain, sustenance and tenant; Latin sub- gives the upward support. The develop element is French and its second part is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 tenere「握住」衍生 sustain、sustenance 与 tenant；拉丁 sub- 提供向上支撑义。develop 成分来自法语，其第二部分来源不确定。

items.structure: Latin prefix sub- 'under, up from below'
items.example: The prefix puts the support beneath the load.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把支撑放在重物之下。

items.example: The root supplies the idea of holding firm.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「稳稳握住」的意思。

items.structure: Latin sustinere via Old French sustenir
items.example: The soil sustains the crop for one season.
A yield that can be sustained is sustainable.
items.exampleCN: 能维持下去的产量就是可持续的。
这个农场采用可持续的方法。

items.example: Sustainability is the state of being able to continue.
items.exampleCN: sustainability 就是能够延续的状态。

items.example: The audit measured sustainability of the harvest.
items.exampleCN: 审计衡量了采获的可持续性。

items.example: The town developed along the river.
items.exampleCN: 这座城镇沿河发展起来。

items.example: The city adopted a sustainable development plan.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市通过了可持续发展规划。
这种用水方式不可持续。

definition_zh: 脆的，易碎的；脆弱的，靠不住的；（声音）尖利的
definition_en: hard but liable to break easily; fragile in temper or health; sharp and crackling in sound
core_image: 玻璃般的硬壳，一敲就裂出细纹
scene: 深秋的凉台上，老人捏着一片枯叶轻轻一折。 The dry leaf turned brittle and snapped in her fingers.
sceneCN: 这里 brittle 是「脆的、易碎的」（第 1 个义项：硬而无韧，一折即断）；句意是干枯的叶子发脆，在她指间啪地断了。

pos.zh: 脆的；易碎的；脆弱的；（声音）尖利刺耳的

derivatives.zh: 由 brittle 加 -ness 构成，义为「脆性；脆弱」
由 brittle 加 -ly 构成，义为「发脆地；尖利地（罕用）」

senses.title: Hard but easily broken
senses.definition: hard and stiff, but breaking easily under a blow or bend
senses.definitionCN: 硬而僵，但受击或弯折即碎
senses.example: The old paper was so brittle that it cracked at the fold.
senses.exampleCN: 旧纸发脆，一折就裂。
senses.why: The core image is a hard shell with no give inside.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是硬壳内里没有韧劲，一折即断。

senses.title: Easily damaged in health or temper
senses.titleCN: 脆弱的；（体质、情绪）易伤的
senses.definition: fragile, as a person's health, nerves or relationships that break under little pressure
senses.definitionCN: 健康、神经或关系稍受压力便崩溃的脆弱状态
senses.example: After the shock, his nerves grew brittle.
senses.exampleCN: 受惊之后，他的神经变得脆弱。
senses.why: What breaks at a touch in objects extends to what collapses at a touch in people.
senses.whyCN: 物一触即碎的属性，转喻为人一触即溃的状态。

senses.title: Sharp and harsh in sound or manner
senses.definition: having a sharp, crackling or coldly hard quality of sound or manner
senses.definitionCN: 声音干裂刺耳，或态度冷硬生涩
senses.example: She gave a brittle laugh and changed the subject.
senses.exampleCN: 她尖利地笑了一声，随即岔开话题。
senses.why: A brittle surface both snaps and rings; the sound sense copies that snap.
senses.whyCN: 脆物既折断又作响，声音义项模仿的就是这声脆响。

intro.en: Brittle probably grew out of an old word for breaking, related to bretan.
intro.cn: brittle 一般认为由古英语表「碎裂」的词派生而来。

items.en: brytan meant to shatter or crush to pieces.
items.cn: 古英语 brytan 意为击碎、碾碎。

items.en: britel meant liable to break, a diminutive of the breaking verb.
items.cn: 中古英语 britel 意为易碎的，由碎裂动词加指小后缀构成。

items.en: spelling settled as brittle; the word spread to temper and sound.
items.cn: 拼写定型为 brittle，词义扩展到性情与声音。

items.en: materials science fixed brittle as the technical opposite of ductile.
items.cn: 材料科学把 brittle 定为 ductile（延展性）的技术反义词。

items.en: brittle covers glass, bones, nerves and laughs.
items.cn: 如今 brittle 可形容玻璃、骨骼、神经与笑声。

note.en: Brittle sits among breaking words and stands against bendable ones.
note.cn: brittle 处于一组碎裂词之间，并与可弯折词相对。

entries.definition: short stiff hairs; to stand up in anger
entries.definitionCN: 刚毛；（毛发）竖起——只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: the quality of being brittle
entries.definitionCN: 脆性，由 brittle 派生的名词

entries.definition: a northern dialect form of brittle
entries.definitionCN: brittle 的北方方言变体

entries.definition: easily broken or damaged
entries.definitionCN: 易碎的；脆弱的，侧重需轻拿轻放

entries.definition: weak and delicate
entries.definitionCN: 虚弱纤弱的，多形容人或身体

entries.definition: firm and breaking with a clean snap
entries.definitionCN: 酥脆的，常含悦耳爽口之意

entries.definition: able to be stretched without breaking
entries.definitionCN: 有延展性的，brittle 的技术反义词

entries.definition: to break suddenly into pieces
entries.definitionCN: 粉碎；碎裂，brittle 之物的下场

normalIntro.en: Hold brittle against bristle to keep the two straight.
normalIntro.cn: 把 brittle 与 bristle 对照着记，避免混淆。

normal.en: Brittle has TT like a crack splitting the word.
normal.cn: brittle 的双写 tt 像一道裂纹把词劈开。

normal.en: Bristle is hair; brittle is glass.
normal.cn: bristle 是硬毛，brittle 是玻璃。

normal.en: Brittle bones break: the old fear of age.
normal.cn: brittle bones（脆骨）是年老的旧忧。

normal.en: Crisp snaps sweetly; brittle snaps badly.
normal.cn: crisp 脆得悦耳，brittle 脆得糟心。

normal.en: Ductile bends, brittle breaks.
normal.cn: ductile 能弯，brittle 会断。

abstract.en: Hear one dry leaf crack between two fingers.
abstract.cn: 听一片枯叶在指间断裂。

abstract.en: See the hairline zigzag run across old varnish.
abstract.cn: 看见旧漆面上细裂纹蜿蜒而过。

abstract.en: Feel a laugh with nothing warm under it.
abstract.cn: 体会笑声底下毫无暖意的感觉。

examples.en: Handle the brittle old manuscript with cotton gloves.
examples.cn: 戴棉手套翻动发脆的旧手稿。

examples.en: Their truce proved brittle and collapsed within weeks.
examples.cn: 休战证明是脆弱的，几周内便告破裂。

examples.en: He answered in a brittle voice that hid his nerves.
examples.cn: 他以尖硬的声音作答，掩饰着内心的紧张。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「玻璃透」——brittle 像「玻璃」一样硬而「透」脆，一磕就裂。

root: brittle 一般认为源自古英语 brytan（击碎），中古英语 britel 由该动词加指小后缀 -el 构成，义为「易碎的」；更早词根来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: From breaking under the hand, the word moves to breaking under stress, then to a snap in voice and manner.
sensesIntro.cn: 从手感之下的断裂，到压力之下的崩溃，再到声音态度里的干硬脆响。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hard shell cracking at the first blow.
core.cn: 核心意象：硬壳一敲即裂。

branches.en: brittle plastic
branches.cn: 脆性塑料

branches.en: brittle old bones
branches.cn: 脆弱的老年骨骼

branches.en: brittle relations
branches.cn: 脆弱的关系

branches.en: a brittle laugh
branches.cn: 尖利的笑声

branches.en: brittle and near tears
branches.cn: 强撑着几乎落泪

intro.en: Brittle is a small family: an abstract noun and a rare adverb.
intro.cn: brittle 词族很小：一个抽象名词，一个罕用副词。

latinIntro.en: The root is Germanic; its technical opposite is Latin-born ductile.
latinIntro.cn: 词根属日耳曼语族；其技术反义词 ductile 则出自拉丁语。

definition_zh: 移民入境；（总称）入境移民；入境查验
definition_en: the act or process of coming to a country in order to live there, or the flow of people who do so
core_image: 机场到达口一条长队，行李箱贴着不同颜色的标签，玻璃门后是等候接机的家人
scene: 海关大厅里，一家人提着行李箱排在队伍末端，孩子紧紧抓着护照。 Immigration has reshaped the neighbourhood's shops and schools.
sceneCN: 这里 immigration 指「人口迁入一个国家并定居的过程」（第 1 个义项：入境定居这一行为）；句意为移民入境改变了这个街区的店铺与学校。图中可辨识物件：到达口长队、贴标签的行李箱、护照、接机的人群。

pos.zh: 移民入境；入境移民（不可数；指具体批次时可作可数）

senses.title: The act of settling in a new country
senses.titleCN: 迁入他国并定居的行为
senses.definition: the act of coming to a country that is not one's own in order to live there
senses.definitionCN: 来到并非自己所属的国家并在此生活的行为
senses.example: Immigration has reshaped the neighbourhood's shops and schools.
senses.exampleCN: 移民入境改变了这个街区的店铺与学校。
senses.why: the prefix means into and the root means to move, so immigration is movement inward, seen from the receiving country.
senses.whyCN: 前缀意为「进入」，词根意为「迁移」，因此 immigration 是从接收国角度看到的向内移动。

senses.title: The volume of people arriving
senses.titleCN: 入境移民的总量与流量
senses.definition: the number or flow of people entering a country over a period
senses.definitionCN: 一段时间内进入一国的人数或人流
senses.example: Immigration doubled in the decade after the mines opened.
senses.exampleCN: 矿区开工后的十年里，入境移民数量翻了一番。
senses.why: an uncountable noun easily turns into a quantity word, as with traffic or rainfall.
senses.whyCN: 不可数名词很容易转为数量词，就像「交通量」或「降雨量」那样。

senses.title: The border admission process
senses.definition: the official procedure by which a country admits or refuses entrants
senses.definitionCN: 一国准许或拒绝入境者的官方程序
senses.example: The queue at immigration stretched past the baggage hall.
senses.exampleCN: 入境查验的队伍一直排到行李厅之外。
senses.why: the abstract noun metonymically names the desk and the officers that carry the process out.
senses.whyCN: 抽象名词以转喻方式指执行这一程序的服务台与官员。

senses.title: Immigrants taken as a group
senses.definition: the people who have entered a country, considered collectively
senses.definitionCN: 已经进入一国的人，作为整体来看
senses.example: Immigration built the city's garment trade in two generations.
senses.exampleCN: 入境移民在两代人之内建起了这座城市的制衣业。
senses.why: the act stands for the actors, a common shortcut in political speech.
senses.whyCN: 用行为指代行为者，是政治语言中常见的省略。

senses.title: A component of population change
senses.definition: the gain of people from abroad in the accounting of a population
senses.definitionCN: 在人口核算中来自国外的净增人数
senses.example: Natural increase fell, so immigration kept the population growing.
senses.exampleCN: 自然增长下降，因此移民入境维持了人口增长。
senses.why: demographers balance births, deaths, immigration and emigration, and each one is a line in the ledger.
senses.whyCN: 人口学者在出生、死亡、迁入与迁出之间做平衡，每一项都是账簿上的一行。

senses.title: Colonization by a species
senses.definition: the arrival of organisms into a habitat where they were not previously established
senses.definitionCN: 生物进入此前并未立足的栖息地
senses.example: Immigration of new species followed the opening of the canal.
senses.exampleCN: 运河开通之后，新物种随之迁入。
senses.why: ecology borrows the word because individuals arriving and settling is the same pattern at a different scale.
senses.whyCN: 生态学借用这个词，因为个体到来并定居，是同一格局在不同尺度上的表现。

senses.title: A historical wave or era
senses.titleCN: 历史上的移民潮与时代
senses.definition: a distinct period or wave in which large numbers of people entered a country
senses.definitionCN: 大批人口进入某国的特定时期或浪潮
senses.example: The great immigration of the 1880s left its mark on the census.
senses.exampleCN: 19 世纪 80 年代的移民大潮在普查中留下了印记。
senses.why: historians turn the process into a countable event when a wave has a clear beginning and end.
senses.whyCN: 当一次浪潮起止清楚时，历史学者会把这一过程变成可计数的事件。

senses.title: A political issue
senses.titleCN: 作为政治议题的移民问题
senses.definition: the framing of entry and settlement as a matter of public dispute and policy
senses.definitionCN: 把入境与定居框定为公共争论与政策问题
senses.example: Immigration dominated the debate in every constituency.
senses.exampleCN: 移民问题在每一个选区都主导了辩论。
senses.why: once the word becomes a topic rather than an event, it can dominate an election without naming any person.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词成为议题而非事件，它就能在未指名任何人的情况下主导一场选举。

intro.en: Immigration rests on Latin immigrare 'to move into', from in- 'into' plus migrare 'to depart, migrate'. The English noun appeared in the seventeenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: immigration 源于拉丁 immigrare「迁入」，由 in-「进入」与 migrare「离开、迁移」构成。英语名词出现于 17 世纪。年代均为约数。

items.en: Migrare meant 'to move from one place to another, to change residence'. Its own earlier origin is not established, and the Indo-European root sometimes proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: migrare 意为「从一处移到另一处、更换居所」。它更早的来源未得到证明，常为其提出的印欧词根属重构形式。

items.en: The preposition in 'into' became a prefix marking motion inward, the mirror of e- or ex- marking motion out.
items.cn: 介词 in「进入」成为前缀，标记向内的移动，与标记向外移动的 e- 或 ex- 正相对。

items.en: In- plus migrare gave immigrare 'to move into a place, to settle there', used of people and later of animals.
items.cn: in- 加 migrare 构成 immigrare「迁入某地并定居」，用于人，后来也用于动物。

items.en: English formed immigration from the stem of immigrate in the seventeenth century, at first for settlement within a country as well as across borders.
items.cn: 英语在 17 世纪用 immigrate 的词干构成 immigration，最初既指跨国入境，也指一国之内的迁居。

items.en: Border controls and mass shipping in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries narrowed the word to entry into a state, and made it a standard term of policy and demography.
items.cn: 19 与 20 世纪的边境管控与大规模航运，把这个词收窄为进入国家，并使其成为政策与人口学的标准术语。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Latin history of migrare is unsettled, and the earliest English citation of the noun is not precisely fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：migrare 在拉丁语之前的历史尚无定论，这个名词的最早英语书证也没有精确年代。

note.en: Group one holds the near-identical migration words that differ only by direction; group two holds words for arrival and settlement.
note.cn: 第一组是只差方向的迁移类近形词；第二组是表示到来与定居的说法。

entries.definition: The same movement seen from the country people leave, with e- 'out' instead of in- 'into'.
entries.definitionCN: 同一移动从人们离开的国家看，前缀为「向外」而非「向内」。

entries.definition: Movement from one place to another without specifying whether a border is crossed; it covers birds, workers and data.
entries.definitionCN: 从一地到另一地的移动，不说明是否越过国境；可指鸟类、劳动者与数据。

entries.definition: The person who immigrates; the noun of action and the noun of person are constantly swapped in speech.
entries.definitionCN: 迁入的人；表动作的名词与表人的名词在口语中常被互换。

entries.definition: The person who emigrates, named from the sending side; the same individual can be both terms at once.
entries.definitionCN: 迁出的人，从输出方命名；同一个人可以同时是两个称呼。

entries.definition: A mass arrival of people, money or things; it stresses volume and suddenness rather than the legal act.
entries.definitionCN: 人、钱或物的大量涌入；强调数量与突然性，而非法律行为。

entries.definition: The process of making a permanent home in a new place; it can follow immigration but is not the crossing itself.
entries.definitionCN: 在新地方安家的过程；可以发生在移民之后，但不等于越境本身。

entries.definition: The instant of reaching a place; it says nothing about staying or about official permission.
entries.definitionCN: 到达某地的那一刻；不涉及是否留下或是否获准。

entries.definition: A planned move to a new place, often arranged by authorities for refugees; it is a policy channel of immigration.
entries.definitionCN: 有计划的迁往新地，常由当局为难民安排；是移民入境的一种政策渠道。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real prefix, the real root and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的前缀、真实的词根与真实的固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The prefix means into and the root means move: movement inward.
normal.cn: 前缀意为进入，词根意为迁移：向内的移动。

normal.en: The pair immigration and emigration differ only in the direction of the prefix.
normal.cn: 移民入境与移民出境这一对词，只差前缀的方向。

normal.en: The person noun adds a ending for the one who does it.
normal.cn: 表人的名词加一个表施动者的词尾，指做这件事的人。

normal.en: Fixed phrases such as immigration policy and immigration control belong to the border sense.
normal.cn: 移民政策、入境管控这类固定搭配属于边境义。

normal.en: In demography it is one line in the ledger beside births and deaths.
normal.cn: 在人口学中，它是出生与死亡旁边账簿上的一行。

abstract.en: Picture a one-way door that only opens from the outside.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇单向门，只能从外面推开。

abstract.en: Picture a river splitting into two channels, one called in and one called out.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河分成两条水道，一条叫进，一条叫出。

abstract.en: Picture a household ledger where one column is arrivals and the opposite column departures.
abstract.cn: 想象一本家庭账簿，一栏记到来，对面一栏记离开。

examples.en: Immigration rose sharply after the labour shortage of the 1950s.
examples.cn: 20 世纪 50 年代劳动力短缺之后，移民入境急剧上升。

examples.en: The ministry published immigration figures for the first quarter.
examples.cn: 该部门公布了第一季度的移民入境数字。

examples.en: Students queued at immigration for nearly two hours.
examples.cn: 学生们在入境查验处排了近两个小时的队。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一民·进来」——一批人进来定居，就是移民入境

root: 拉丁 in-「进入」+ migrare「迁移」→ immigrare「迁入定居」；英语 immigration 于 17 世纪由 immigrate 的词干构成。migrare 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement seen from the receiving side: the act of entry, the volume of arrivals, the desk that checks them, the people themselves, the line in the population ledger, the arrival of a species, a historical wave and a political issue.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从接收方看到的同一次移动展开：入境的行为、到来者的总量、查验的服务台、这些人本身、人口账簿上的一行、物种的到来、历史浪潮与政治议题。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a queue at an arrival gate, each suitcase carrying a life that is about to be unpacked somewhere else.
core.cn: 核心意象：到达口的一条长队，每只行李箱里都装着一段即将在别处展开的生活。

branches.en: CROSSING: the base act of coming in order to stay.
branches.cn: 越境而入：为了留下而进来的基础行为。

branches.en: VOLUME AND WAVE: the flow can be counted, and a counted flow becomes a historical wave.
branches.cn: 总量与浪潮：流量可以被计数，而被计数的流量会成为历史浪潮。

branches.en: CHECKPOINT: the abstract noun stands for the desk and the officers who carry the process out.
branches.cn: 查验口：抽象名词指执行该程序的服务台与官员。

branches.en: THE ARRIVING: people taken as a group, and, in ecology, organisms colonizing a habitat.
branches.cn: 到来者：作为整体的人，以及在生态学中定殖栖息的生物。

branches.en: LEDGER AND DEBATE: one line in population accounting, and one topic in public argument.
branches.cn: 账簿与争论：人口核算中的一行，也是公共争论中的一个议题。

intro.en: Immigration is a prefix, a root and a suffix, and the same pieces build the whole migration family.
intro.cn: immigration 由一个前缀、一个词根与一个后缀构成，同样的成分也构成整个迁移词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin in- marks motion inward, migrare supplies the root of moving, and -ation turns the verb into an action noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 in- 标记向内移动，migrare 提供「迁移」的词根，-ation 把动词变成表动作的名词。

items.example: The prefix directs the movement toward the receiving country.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把移动朝向接收国。

items.meaning: move from one place to another
items.example: The root supplies the idea of changing residence.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供更换居所的意思。
她的祖父母在 20 世纪 30 年代迁入。

items.example: It builds the person noun from the verb.
items.exampleCN: 它由动词构成表人的名词。

items.meaning: a person who moves into a country
items.example: The first immigrant on the list arrived in 1848.
items.exampleCN: 名单上的第一位移民于 1848 年抵达。

items.example: It turns the verb into the name of the process.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变成过程之名。

items.meaning: the process of moving into a country
items.example: Immigration filled the mills with new workers.
items.exampleCN: 移民入境为工厂填满了新工人。

items.example: The opposite prefix names the same movement from the other end.
items.exampleCN: 相反的前缀从另一端为同一移动命名。

items.meaning: to move out of a country
items.example: The family emigrated in search of work.
items.exampleCN: 这家人为寻找工作而迁出。

definition_zh: adj. 秃头的；无发的；光秃的、磨平的；（陈述）直白的、不加掩饰的
definition_en: having little or no hair on the scalp; lacking natural covering or detail; plain and blunt, without softening
core_image: 帽子摘下后那片反着光的头顶
scene: 他摘下帽子，露出光亮的前额。 He took off his cap and showed a bald crown that caught the light.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：bald 指头上无发；句意是他摘帽后露出反光的秃顶。

senses.title: Without hair
senses.definition: having little or no hair on the head
senses.definitionCN: 头上很少或没有头发
senses.example: He went bald in his early thirties.
senses.exampleCN: 他三十出头就秃了。
senses.why: The Middle English form described a shining white patch on the head, and the sense narrowed to the bareness itself.
senses.whyCN: 中古英语形式描写头上一块发亮的白斑，词义后来收窄为「光秃」本身。

senses.title: Stripped of covering
senses.definition: lacking the natural or usual covering, such as hair, tread, or vegetation
senses.definitionCN: 缺少天然或惯常的覆盖物，如毛发、胎面花纹或植被
senses.example: The tyres were bald and the hillside was bare.
senses.exampleCN: 轮胎花纹磨平了，山坡也光秃秃的。
senses.why: Once bald means bare skin, any surface that has lost its layer can borrow the word.
senses.whyCN: 既然 bald 指裸露的皮肤，任何失去表层的表面都能借用这个词。

senses.title: Plain and blunt
senses.definition: stated without any attempt to soften or disguise it
senses.definitionCN: 陈述时不作任何缓和或掩饰
senses.example: It was a bald lie and everyone knew it.
senses.exampleCN: 那是个赤裸裸的谎言，人人都看得出来。
senses.why: Speech with nothing laid over it is bare in the same way as a head with no hair.
senses.whyCN: 不加覆盖的言语，与不长头发的头一样「赤裸」。

intro.en: Bald probably began as a word about colour, not hair: a shining white patch. From there it moved to bareness, and then to blunt speech.
intro.cn: bald 起初大概是讲颜色而非头发：一块发亮的白斑。由此转为「光秃」，再转为「言语直白」。

items.en: The root bhel meant to shine or gleam white, and it also gives blaze and bleach.
items.cn: 词根 bhel 意为发亮或呈白色，也衍生出 blaze 与 bleach。

items.en: Middle English balled describes a head marked by a shining white patch.
items.cn: 中古英语 balled 形容头上有一块发亮的白斑。

items.en: Welsh bal names a white streak on the forehead of a horse, a close match in sense.
items.cn: 威尔士语 bal 指马额上的白色条纹，词义十分接近。

items.en: The spelling settles as bald, and the meaning shifts from white patch to hairless.
items.cn: 拼写定为 bald，词义由「白斑」转为「无发」。

items.en: Writers use the word for any surface stripped of its natural cover, such as a bald hill.
items.cn: 文人用该词指任何失去天然覆盖的表面，如光秃的山丘。

items.en: A figurative sense grows: the word now marks a statement left blunt and unsoftened.
items.cn: 又生出比喻义：该词指陈述直白、不加缓和修饰。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on one-letter and one-vowel neighbours, bold above all; the near-meaning group splits into bare surfaces and blunt speech, matching the two extended senses.
note.cn: 形近组由只差一个字母或一个元音的邻居组成，尤其是 bold；近义组分为「裸露表面」与「言语直白」两支，正对应两个引申义。

entries.definition: Confident and willing to take risks.
entries.definitionCN: 大胆的；无畏的。

entries.definition: A round object used in games.
entries.definitionCN: 球；圆球状物。

entries.definition: A large bound bundle of hay or paper.
entries.definitionCN: 一大捆干草或废纸。

entries.definition: To shout or weep noisily.
entries.definitionCN: 大喊；号哭。

entries.definition: Having no hair on a normally hairy part.
entries.definitionCN: 本应有毛处无毛的。

entries.definition: Without covering or clothing.
entries.definitionCN: 裸露的；无遮盖的。

entries.definition: With hair removed by a razor.
entries.definitionCN: 剃过的；刮净的。

entries.definition: Direct in speech, sometimes rudely so.
entries.definitionCN: 说话直率的，有时近于无礼。

normalIntro.en: Bald and bold differ by one vowel: bold is a full head of courage, bald is an empty head of hair.
normalIntro.cn: bald 与 bold 只差一个元音：bold 是满头勇气，bald 是满头无发。

normal.en: See the a in bald and think of a bare scalp.
normal.cn: 看到 bald 里的 a，就想一片空空的头皮。

normal.en: A bald tyre has lost its tread, just as a head loses hair.
normal.cn: bald tyre 是花纹磨光的轮胎，正如头掉了头发。

normal.en: A bald statement has no covering words.
normal.cn: bald statement 是没有修饰词遮盖的陈述。

normal.en: Balder and baldest are the regular comparisons.
normal.cn: 比较级 balder、最高级 baldest 都是规则变化。

normal.en: Baldness is the state, baldly is the manner.
normal.cn: baldness 是状态，baldly 是方式。

abstract.en: A surface with nothing left to hide behind.
abstract.cn: 一个再无遮蔽可依的表面。

abstract.en: Truth without its usual coat.
abstract.cn: 没穿惯常外衣的真话。

abstract.en: Time taking away a layer nobody asked it to take.
abstract.cn: 时间取走了一层谁也没让它取的东西。

examples.en: His bald head shone under the office lights.
examples.cn: 他的秃头在办公室灯下发亮。

examples.en: The report gave a bald account of the losses.
examples.cn: 报告对损失作了毫不掩饰的陈述。

examples.en: Bald patches appeared where the sheep had grazed.
examples.cn: 羊啃过的地方出现了一块块秃斑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 对比记忆：bold「大胆」把 o 换成 a 就成了 bald「秃的」——胆子鼓鼓是 bold，头顶空空是 bald。再串三层：头顶无发 → 表面无覆盖 → 说话无修饰。

root: 可能源自原始印欧语词根 bhel「发亮、白」，中古英语约 1300 年作 balled，指头上发亮的白斑；威尔士语 bal「马额白纹」为旁证。15 世纪拼写定为 bald 并转指无发，17 世纪扩为一切光秃表面，19 世纪再扩为言语直白。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses, one idea: a surface with its covering gone, whether that covering is hair, tread, or polite wording.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项，一个念头：覆盖物消失后的表面——不论那覆盖物是头发、胎面花纹，还是客套的措辞。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cap lifted off a shining bare crown
core.cn: 核心意象：帽子从反光的秃顶上被揭开

branches.en: A razor drawn over the scalp.
branches.cn: 剃刀刮过头皮。

branches.en: A tyre worn smooth to the casing.
branches.cn: 磨到露出胎体的光轮胎。

branches.en: A hillside cropped to the soil.
branches.cn: 啃到露土的山坡。

branches.en: A lie with no wrapper.
branches.cn: 没有包装的谎言。

branches.en: Nothing left on top.
branches.cn: 上面什么也不剩。

intro.en: Bald is a bare adjective root; the useful endings are the comparison pair and the suffixes that turn it into a state or a manner.
intro.cn: bald 是一个赤裸的形容词词根；有用的词尾是比较级最高级这一对，以及把它变成状态或方式的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the learned synonyms rather than the word itself: calvus for bald and glaber for smooth and hairless.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供的是书面近义表达而非该词本身：calvus 表「秃」，glaber 表「光滑无毛」。

latinEntries.exampleCN: Calvus 曾是罗马人的绰号。

definition_zh: n. 贝雷帽（扁圆无檐的软帽，多为毛料）；军帽（以颜色标示兵种）
definition_en: a soft round flat cap without a peak, usually of wool; a coloured cap worn by soldiers to show their unit
core_image: 画家把沾着颜料的扁圆软帽往脑后一推
scene: 画家把沾着颜料的贝雷帽往脑后一推。 The painter pushed his paint-stained beret back on his head.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：beret 指扁圆无檐的软帽；句意是画家把沾了颜料的贝雷帽往脑后推。

senses.title: The soft flat cap
senses.definition: a soft round cap with no peak, made of wool or felt and worn flat on the head
senses.definitionCN: 无檐的圆形软帽，用毛料或毡制，平戴在头上
senses.example: He rolled the beret and put it in his pocket.
senses.exampleCN: 他把贝雷帽卷起来塞进口袋。
senses.why: The word travelled from a hooded cloak to a head covering, and the cloak is long gone.
senses.whyCN: 该词从带风帽的斗篷转到头部覆盖物，而斗篷早已不在。

senses.title: The soldier cap
senses.definition: a coloured beret worn by a regiment as its badge of identity
senses.definitionCN: 以颜色标识部队身份的军用作训帽
senses.example: The green beret marked the unit before any badge.
senses.exampleCN: 在看清徽章之前，绿贝雷帽已经说明了兵种。
senses.why: Because the cap is plain, colour carries all the meaning, and armies turned it into a uniform sign.
senses.whyCN: 帽子本身素净，意义全由颜色承担，军队便把它变成了制服符号。

intro.en: Beret began as a hooded cloak, became a shepherd flat cap in the Pyrenees, and then a soldier badge of colour.
intro.cn: beret 起初是带风帽的斗篷，后来在比利牛斯成了牧人的扁帽，最后成为军中以色区分的标志。

items.en: Late Latin birrus names a thick cloak with a hood, probably a Celtic word.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 birrus 指带风帽的厚斗篷，可能源自凯尔特语。

items.en: Medieval Latin birretum shifts from cloak to the head covering itself.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 birretum 由斗篷转为指头部覆盖物。

items.en: Gascon berret names a flat round cap worn by Basque and Pyrenean shepherds.
items.cn: 加斯科涅语 berret 指巴斯克与比利牛斯牧人戴的扁平圆帽。

items.en: French béret spreads the word as the Basque cap becomes widely worn.
items.cn: 法语 béret 随巴斯克帽的流行把该词传开。

items.en: French and British units adopt coloured berets, and the word enters army use.
items.cn: 法英部队采用彩色贝雷帽，该词进入军队用语。

items.en: English adopts the word for the soft flat cap, often with an artistic air.
items.cn: 英语借入该词指软扁圆帽，常带艺术气息。

note.en: The look-alike group holds short be-/be- words that are spelled close but unrelated; the near-meaning group lists the other soft caps the beret sits among.
note.cn: 形近组放拼写相近却无关的短 be- 词；近义组列出与贝雷帽同类的其他软帽。

entries.definition: To tell someone off angrily and long.
entries.definitionCN: 长时间愤怒地斥责。

entries.definition: Deprived of something valued.
entries.definitionCN: 失去珍贵之物。

entries.definition: A pale green gem.
entries.definitionCN: 浅绿色宝石。

entries.definition: A small juicy fruit.
entries.definitionCN: 小而多汁的果实。

entries.definition: A soft head covering, often with a peak.
entries.definitionCN: 常有帽檐的软帽。

entries.definition: A hat tied under the chin.
entries.definitionCN: 系在下巴下的帽子。

entries.definition: A round wool cap with a pompom.
entries.definitionCN: 带绒球的圆毛帽。

entries.definition: A red cylindrical hat with a tassel.
entries.definitionCN: 带流苏的红色圆柱帽。

normalIntro.en: Beret is a French word for a Basque shepherd cap. No peak, no brim, just a soft disc of wool.
normalIntro.cn: beret 是一个法语词，指巴斯克牧人的帽子。无檐、无舌，只是一片柔软的羊毛圆盘。

normal.en: No peak, no brim: you can fold it flat.
normal.cn: 无檐无舌，可以折平。

normal.en: French béret came from a Gascon word for the cap.
normal.cn: 法语 béret 出自加斯科涅语中的帽名。

normal.en: A green beret is a whole regiment in one colour.
normal.cn: 一顶绿贝雷帽就是一个兵种。

normal.en: Berets is the plural, -s only.
normal.cn: 复数是 berets，只加 -s。

normal.en: It began as a cloak with a hood, not a cap.
normal.cn: 它起初指带风帽的斗篷，而非帽子。

abstract.en: A circle of wool that tells you who someone is.
abstract.cn: 一片能说明你身份的羊毛圆盘。

abstract.en: Art worn where it can be seen.
abstract.cn: 穿在看得见处的艺术。

abstract.en: A colour doing the work of a uniform.
abstract.cn: 由一种颜色承担的制服功能。

examples.en: She pinned a silver brooch to her beret.
examples.cn: 她在贝雷帽上别了一枚银胸针。

examples.en: The recruits were issued blue berets on day one.
examples.cn: 新兵第一天就领到了蓝色贝雷帽。

examples.en: He wore the beret pulled down over one ear.
examples.cn: 他把贝雷帽斜拉下来盖住一只耳朵。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「贝蕾」——像一枚柔软的贝蕾圆片，无檐无舌，就是 beret 贝雷帽。联想两支场景：画家的沾色软帽，士兵的彩色军帽。

root: 经由法语 béret 上溯加斯科涅语 berret，再上溯中世纪拉丁语 birretum，最终到晚期拉丁语 birrus「带风帽的厚斗篷」，可能源自凯尔特语。19 世纪随巴斯克帽流行而西传，1918 年前后进入军队用语，1930 年代在英语中定型。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses, one cap: the plain wool disc everyone wears, and the coloured version an army uses as a name tag.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项，同一顶帽：人人可戴的素色羊毛圆盘，以及军队当名牌用的彩色版。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flat wool disc pushed back off the forehead
core.cn: 核心意象：被推到额头上方的扁平羊毛圆片

branches.en: A paint mark on the wool.
branches.cn: 羊毛上的一处颜料。

branches.en: A beret rolled into a pocket.
branches.cn: 卷起来塞进口袋的贝雷帽。

branches.en: A green disc above a badge.
branches.cn: 徽章上方的一片绿。

branches.en: Recruits filing past with new caps.
branches.cn: 新兵戴着新帽列队走过。

branches.en: Shape first, colour later.
branches.cn: 先有形，后有颜色。

intro.en: Beret is a borrowed whole word; the useful parts are its Latin ancestor birrus and the small French endings around it.
intro.cn: beret 是整体借入的词；有用的构件是它的拉丁语祖先 birrus，以及围绕它的法语小词尾。

latinIntro.en: Late Latin birrus means a hooded cloak and Medieval Latin birretum means a cap; caput, head, is the other Latin thread here.
latinIntro.cn: 晚期拉丁语 birrus 意为带风帽的斗篷，中世纪拉丁语 birretum 意为帽；caput「头」是这里另一条拉丁线索。

definition_zh: 导航；航行；确定位置并找到路线的过程，也指网页或系统的导览结构
definition_en: the process of finding a position and a route, the act of sailing, or the menu structure that guides users through a site
core_image: 船在无岸的海上凭星位与海图校正方向，一步步靠近港口
scene: 浓雾里看不见岸，船长靠罗盘方位和灯塔的间隔校正航向，慢慢贴近港口。 With no shore in sight, the captain corrects the course by compass bearing and the spacing of lighthouses, a patient art of navigation.
sceneCN: 这里 navigation 指「确定位置并找到航线的过程」（第 2 个义项：靠方位与地标不断校正）；句意为浓雾中看不见岸，船长凭罗盘与灯塔间距修正航向，慢慢驶近港口。图中可辨识物件：罗盘、海图、灯塔、雾中的船首；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 航行；导航；导览结构（不可数）

senses.title: Sailing on water
senses.definition: the act of sailing or steering a vessel along a route
senses.definitionCN: 驾驶船只沿航线行驶的行为
senses.example: Navigation on the river began before roads were built.
senses.exampleCN: 这条路还没有修好之前，河上航行就已开始。
senses.why: navis 'ship' plus agere 'drive' is literally ship-driving, so the oldest sense is the movement of a hull through water.
senses.whyCN: navis「船」加 agere「驾驶」，字面就是「驾船」；最古老的含义正是船体在水上的移动。

senses.title: Position fixing and route finding
senses.definition: the process of determining where one is and which course leads to the destination
senses.definitionCN: 确定自己在哪里、哪条航线通向目的地的过程
senses.example: The captain corrected the course by compass and lighthouses.
senses.exampleCN: 船长凭罗盘与灯塔校正了航向。
senses.why: the core of navigation is two questions, where am I and where next; every instrument serves one of them.
senses.whyCN: 导航的核心是两个问题：我在哪里、下一步往哪；每件仪器都在为其中之一服务。

senses.title: Website navigation
senses.definition: the menus, links and layout that let a user move through a site or app
senses.definitionCN: 让用户在网站或应用中移动的菜单、链接与布局
senses.example: Clear navigation kept visitors from leaving the site.
senses.exampleCN: 清晰的导航让访客没有离开网站。
senses.why: a user is also a traveller: the menu is a chart of the site, and a bad chart produces the digital equivalent of being lost.
senses.whyCN: 用户也是行者：菜单是网站的海图，海图糟糕就会产生数字版的迷路。

senses.title: Animal navigation
senses.definition: the ability of animals to orient and travel toward a goal over long distances
senses.definitionCN: 动物辨向并长距离前往目标的能力
senses.example: Monarch butterflies manage navigation across a continent.
senses.exampleCN: 帝王蝶能完成跨大陆的导航。
senses.why: biology uses the word because the same two questions apply without instruments: where am I, and which way is home.
senses.whyCN: 生物学使用这个词，因为同样两个问题在没有仪器时也成立：我在哪，家在哪边。

senses.title: Air and space navigation
senses.definition: plotting and correcting a course through the air or in orbit
senses.definitionCN: 在空中或轨道上规划并修正航线
senses.example: Space navigation relies on signals from ground stations.
senses.exampleCN: 航天导航依赖地面站信号。
senses.why: as the medium changes, the instruments change, but the loop of fix, compare and correct remains.
senses.whyCN: 介质改变，仪器随之改变，但「定位、比对、修正」的循环不变。

senses.title: Navigation technology
senses.definition: the instruments and systems that support positioning and routing
senses.definitionCN: 支持定位与选路的仪器与系统
senses.example: The app's navigation depends on four satellites.
senses.exampleCN: 这款应用的导航依赖四颗卫星。
senses.why: metonymy lets the activity name its tools, so navigation can mean the equipment that makes it possible.
senses.whyCN: 转喻让活动命名其工具，因此 navigation 也可以指使活动得以进行的设备。

senses.title: Inland waterway transport
senses.definition: the movement of goods or people on rivers and canals
senses.definitionCN: 在河流与运河上运送货物或人员
senses.example: Inland navigation carries coal along the canal.
senses.exampleCN: 内河航运沿运河运送煤炭。
senses.why: the commercial sense narrows the old sailing sense to a transport mode counted in tonnage.
senses.whyCN: 商业义把古老的航行义收窄为一种以吨位计量的运输方式。

senses.title: The science or skill of navigating
senses.definition: the body of knowledge and technique required to find and follow a route
senses.definitionCN: 寻找并沿路线行进所需的知识与技术总体
senses.example: Navigation was taught as a mathematical art.
senses.exampleCN: 导航曾被当作一门数学技艺来教授。
senses.why: a practice that can be taught becomes a discipline, and the noun shifts from doing to knowing how.
senses.whyCN: 可以教授的实践会成为一门学问，名词便从「做」转向「知道怎么做」。

intro.en: Navigation comes from Latin navigatio, from navigare 'to sail', itself navis 'ship' plus agere 'to drive'. It entered English in the sixteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: navigation 来自拉丁 navigatio，源自动词 navigare「航行」，而 navigare 由 navis「船」加 agere「驾驶」构成。它在 16 世纪进入英语。年代为约数。

items.en: Navis meant 'ship, boat'; it belongs to an old Indo-European word for a vessel and survives in navy and in naval.
items.cn: navis 意为「船、舟」；它属于古老的印欧语「船」词，留在 navy 与 naval 中。

items.en: Agere meant 'to drive, lead, do'; it is the verb behind agent, act and agenda.
items.cn: agere 意为「驾驶、引领、做」；它是 agent、act 与 agenda 背后的动词。

items.en: Navis plus agere produced navigare, 'to sail, steer a ship'; the compound is literal, not metaphorical.
items.cn: navis 加 agere 构成 navigare「航行、驾船」；这个复合是字面的，不是比喻。

items.en: The noun navigatio 'a sailing, a voyage' supplied the English word through French in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 名词 navigatio「航行、航程」在 16 世纪经法语提供英语词形。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word extended to animal orientation and to the menus that guide users through software, both treating travel as a path toward a goal.
items.cn: 20 世纪，这个词扩展到动物辨向，以及引导用户使用软件的菜单；两者都把行进当作通往目标的路径。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the earliest English citation is not exactly fixed, and the pre-Indo-European origin of navis is reconstructed rather than attested.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：最早的英语书证没有确切年代；navis 在印欧语之前的来源属于重构，而非直接书证。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same navis plus agere family; group two holds related travel and guidance concepts.
note.cn: 第一组是同一 navis 加 agere 词族的形式；第二组是相关的行进与引导概念。

entries.definition: Relating to navigation; it must modify a noun such as aid or system, while navigation names the activity.
entries.definitionCN: 与导航有关的；必须修饰 aid 或 system 之类名词，而 navigation 命名活动。

entries.definition: Describing water or an aircraft that can be navigated; it judges the route, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 描述可通航的水域或可驾驶的航空器；评判路线，而非动作。

entries.definition: A person who navigates; the -or suffix names the agent, navigation the activity.
entries.definitionCN: 导航的人；-or 后缀命名施动者，navigation 命名活动。

entries.definition: A country's fleet; it comes from navis too, but names the ships as an institution, not the act of steering them.
entries.definitionCN: 一个国家的舰队；同样来自 navis，但把船只作为建制来命名，而非驾驶动作。

entries.definition: Guiding a vessel through a channel by landmarks; it is one branch of navigation, often close to shore.
entries.definitionCN: 凭地标引导船只通过航道；是导航的一支，常发生在近岸。

entries.definition: Finding one's way through a building or city, often by signs; navigation is broader and includes instruments.
entries.definitionCN: 在建筑或城市中认路，常靠标识；navigation 更宽，包含仪器。

entries.definition: Travelling and working at sea; it names a way of life, while navigation names the method.
entries.definitionCN: 在海上旅行与劳作；命名一种生活方式，而 navigation 命名方法。

entries.definition: Choosing the path for data or traffic; it is the technical descendant of route finding.
entries.definitionCN: 为数据或交通选择路径；是找路的技术后裔。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: navis 'ship' + agere 'drive' = drive a ship; the same two roots appear in navy and agent.
normal.cn: navis「船」+ agere「驾驶」= 驾船；同两个词根也出现在 navy 与 agent 中。

normal.en: The family runs navigate, navigator, navigational, navigable and navigability.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 navigate、navigator、navigational、navigable 与 navigability。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: marine navigation, satellite navigation, a navigation system, inland navigation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：海上导航、卫星导航、导航系统、内河航运。

normal.en: Navigation answers two questions: where am I, and which way next.
normal.cn: 导航回答两个问题：我在哪里，下一步往哪。

normal.en: Website navigation borrows the sailor's chart: a menu is a map of pages.
normal.cn: 网页导航借用水手的海图：菜单就是页面的地图。

abstract.en: Picture a small boat with no land in sight, correcting its line by a single star.
abstract.cn: 想象一条看不见陆地的小船，靠一颗星修正航线。

abstract.en: Picture a menu bar as a row of harbour lights, each leading to one page.
abstract.cn: 想象菜单栏像一排港口灯，每盏通向一个页面。

abstract.en: Picture a monarch butterfly that has never seen the destination and still arrives.
abstract.cn: 想象一只从未见过目的地的帝王蝶，仍然抵达。

examples.en: Satellite navigation has replaced paper charts on many ships.
examples.cn: 卫星导航在许多船上取代了纸质海图。

examples.en: The site's navigation was redesigned so that new users could find the help page.
examples.cn: 网站导航经过重新设计，新用户能找到帮助页面。

examples.en: Inland navigation carries more freight than the nearby roads.
examples.cn: 内河航运运送的货物比附近公路更多。

dict_mnemonic.text: navy（船队）+ action（行动）——驾船找路的行动 → 航行、导航

root: 拉丁 navigatio「航行」← navigare「驾船」= navis（船）+ agere（驾驶）；与 navy、agent 同根。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses keep the same loop of fix, compare and correct, but change the traveller: a hull, a walker, a mouse pointer, a butterfly, a spacecraft, an app, a barge and a student of the art.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项保持「定位、比对、修正」的同一循环，只更换行者：船体、行人、鼠标指针、蝴蝶、航天器、应用、驳船，以及学习这门技艺的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: no shore in sight, one bearing checked again and again until the harbour appears.
core.cn: 核心意象：看不见岸，反复校验一个方位，直到港口出现。

branches.en: THE ART: ship-driving as a practice and as a teachable body of knowledge.
branches.cn: 技艺：驾船既是一项实践，也是一套可教授的知识。

branches.en: THE LOOP: fix, compare, correct, whether by star, compass or ground signal.
branches.cn: 循环：定位、比对、修正，不论靠星辰、罗盘还是地面信号。

branches.en: NEW MEDIA: menus and satellite systems inherit the same chart and the same lost user.
branches.cn: 新媒介：菜单与卫星系统继承同样的海图与同样会迷路的使用者。

branches.en: WITHOUT INSTRUMENTS: the butterfly answers the two questions with senses only.
branches.cn: 无仪器：蝴蝶只靠感官回答那两个问题。

branches.en: COMMERCE: the old voyage becomes a transport mode measured in tonnage.
branches.cn: 商业：古老的航程变成以吨位计量的运输方式。

intro.en: Navigation is a Latin compound noun: navis 'ship' plus agere 'drive', then -atio. Both roots have large English families of their own.
intro.cn: navigation 是拉丁复合名词：navis「船」加 agere「驾驶」，再加 -atio。两个词根在英语中各自都有大词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin navis 'ship' and agere 'drive' form navigare and navigatio; English draws navigate, navigator, navigable, navigational and navy from the same stock.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 navis「船」与 agere「驾驶」构成 navigare 与 navigatio；英语由此得到 navigate、navigator、navigable、navigational 与 navy。

items.example: Navis is the source of navy and naval.
items.exampleCN: navis 是 navy 与 naval 的来源。

items.structure: agere, egi, actum (Latin verb, third conjugation)
items.example: Agere also gives agent and agenda.
items.exampleCN: agere 也生成 agent 与 agenda。

items.meaning: the act of sailing or finding a route
items.example: Navigation requires a fix and a course.
items.exampleCN: 导航需要一个定位与一条航线。
她驾船穿过狭窄的航道。

items.example: The navigator plotted the next leg.
items.exampleCN: 领航员标出了下一段航程。

items.meaning: able to be sailed or steered
items.example: The upper river is not navigable in winter.
items.exampleCN: 上游河道冬季不能通航。

items.example: Navigational aids were placed along the coast.
items.exampleCN: 沿海设置了一些导航设施。

items.meaning: a fleet, especially a war fleet

definition_zh: 最佳的；最优的；最适宜的
definition_en: best possible under the given conditions; most favourable
core_image: 一把尺子量到刚刚好，不多一格，也不少一格
scene: 调参的人把三组数值来回试了十几遍，最后停在中间那一组。 That setting gives optimal performance without extra heat.
sceneCN: 这里指各种条件配合到最好（第 1 个义项：在现有条件下最好的结果）；句意为那组设置带来最佳性能，还不会额外发热。

pos.zh: 最佳的；最优的；最适宜的

senses.title: The best possible result
senses.definition: the best outcome available under the present limits
senses.definitionCN: 在现有条件下能得到的最好结果
senses.example: The team reached an optimal result with the given budget.
senses.exampleCN: 团队用既定预算取得了最佳结果。
senses.why: Optimus is the Latin superlative of good, so the word names the top of a scale rather than a direction.
senses.whyCN: optimus 是拉丁语「好」的最高级，因此这个词命名刻度的顶点，而不是某个方向。

senses.title: The most favourable conditions
senses.definition: the conditions under which a process works best
senses.definitionCN: 某过程运作得最好的条件
senses.example: The plants grow at optimal temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 这些植物在最适温度下生长。
senses.why: Once the top of the scale is a point, conditions can be tuned to that point.
senses.whyCN: 一旦刻度的顶点成了一个点，条件就可以调到那一点。

senses.title: A mathematical optimum
senses.definition: a point where a function reaches its best value
senses.definitionCN: 函数取得最好值的点
senses.example: The algorithm searches for an optimal point on the curve.
senses.exampleCN: 算法在曲线上寻找一个最优点。
senses.why: Calculus formalised the everyday top of a scale as a stationary best value.
senses.whyCN: 微积分把日常说的「顶点」形式化为一个驻定的最优值。

senses.title: An efficient economic allocation
senses.definition: the arrangement that uses resources with the least waste
senses.definitionCN: 以最少浪费使用资源的安排
senses.example: The market reached an optimal allocation of labour.
senses.exampleCN: 市场达到了劳动力的最优配置。
senses.why: Economics measures the top by output per unit of input.
senses.whyCN: 经济学用每单位投入的产出来衡量这个顶点。

senses.title: The best dose or timing for the body
senses.titleCN: 对身体最合适的剂量或时机
senses.definition: the amount or moment that does most good and least harm
senses.definitionCN: 收益最大、伤害最小的用量或时点
senses.example: The trial looked for the optimal dose.
senses.exampleCN: 这项试验寻找最佳剂量。
senses.why: Medicine turns the scale into a trade-off between benefit and harm.
senses.whyCN: 医学把这个刻度变成收益与伤害之间的权衡。

senses.title: A settled engineering trade-off
senses.titleCN: 工程上权衡后的最优点
senses.definition: the design point where competing requirements balance best
senses.definitionCN: 各项相争的要求平衡得最好的设计点
senses.example: Weight and strength meet at an optimal thickness.
senses.exampleCN: 重量与强度在某个最佳厚度上取得平衡。
senses.why: Engineering makes the top a compromise rather than a single peak.
senses.whyCN: 工程学让这个顶点成为折中，而不是孤峰。

senses.title: A biological best fit
senses.definition: the behaviour or form that suits an environment best
senses.definitionCN: 最适应某环境的行为或形态
senses.example: The birds show optimal foraging in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 这些鸟在冬季表现出最优觅食。
senses.why: Biology asks what a body or habit is best fitted to, not what is morally best.
senses.whyCN: 生物学问的是身体或习性最适合什么，而非什么在道德上最好。

senses.title: The sensible everyday choice
senses.titleCN: 日常判断中的最佳选择
senses.definition: the choice a careful person judges best overall
senses.definitionCN: 谨慎的人综合判断后认为最好的选择
senses.example: Leaving early was the optimal decision given the traffic.
senses.exampleCN: 考虑到交通，早走是最佳决定。
senses.why: Everyday speech borrows the superlative for a reasoned preference.
senses.whyCN: 日常语言借这个最高级表达有理由的偏好。

intro.en: Optimal comes from Latin optimus, best, the suppletive superlative of bonus, good, with the English suffix -al. The direct source is clear; the deeper origin of optimus is a hypothesis.
intro.cn: optimal 来自拉丁 optimus「最好的」，它是 bonus「好的」的补充式最高级，再加英语后缀 -al。直接来源清楚；optimus 更深的来源是一种假说。

items.en: Bonus meant good, but its comparative melior and superlative optimus came from other stems, a suppletion familiar from good, better, best.
items.cn: bonus 意为好的，但其比较级 melior 与最高级 optimus 来自别的词干，这种补充式与英语 good、better、best 相似。

items.en: Optimus served as best and as most excellent in rank.
items.cn: optimus 既作「最好的」，也指品级上最卓越的。

items.en: Optimus is often connected with ops, resources or power, which would make the earliest sense richest or most able; the derivation is source uncertain.
items.cn: optimus 常与 ops「资源、力量」相联系，若如此则最早义为「最富足」或「最有能力」；这一派生来源不确定。

items.en: The neuter optimum was borrowed as a noun for the best value, especially in mathematics.
items.cn: 中性形式 optimum 被借作名词，指最佳值，尤用于数学。

items.en: English built optimal on optimus in the nineteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪用 optimus 造出 optimal，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Optimisation, suboptimal and optimal control extend the word without changing its peak sense.
items.cn: 最优化、次优与最优控制都沿用这个词，未改变其「顶点」义。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin best-stem; the second group names what sits at the top of a scale.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「最好」的词干；第二组是处在刻度顶端的近义说法。

entries.definition: The best value or point, especially in mathematics.
entries.definitionCN: 最佳值或最优点，尤用于数学。

entries.definition: The belief that things tend toward the best; coined from the Latin optimum.
entries.definitionCN: 相信事物趋向最好的看法；由拉丁 optimum 造出。

entries.definition: To make something as good as it can be; built on optimum.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物尽可能好；由 optimum 构成。

entries.definition: Below the best level, built with the prefix sub-.
entries.definitionCN: 低于最佳水平，由前缀 sub- 构成。

entries.definition: Expecting the best outcome.
entries.definitionCN: 期待最好结果。

entries.definition: The highest in quality or rank; the plain English word.
entries.definitionCN: 质量或等级最高的；最平实的英语说法。

entries.definition: Perfect in an imagined standard, sometimes unattainable.
entries.definitionCN: 符合想象标准的完美，有时难以达到。

entries.definition: Helpful to a plan or outcome.
entries.definitionCN: 对计划或结果有利的。

entries.definition: Of the best quality or at the best moment.
entries.definitionCN: 质量最好的或时机最佳的。

entries.definition: The highest point reached.
entries.definitionCN: 达到的最高点。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin superlative, the real family and real collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁最高级、真实同族词与真实搭配。

normal.en: Optimus is the superlative of bonus, just as best is the superlative of good.
normal.cn: optimus 是 bonus 的最高级，正如英语中「最好」是「好」的最高级。

normal.en: Optimum is the noun for the best value; optimal is the adjective.
normal.cn: optimum 是「最佳值」的名词，optimal 是形容词。

normal.en: The ops hypothesis would make optimus mean richest before it meant best.
normal.cn: 若按 ops 假说，optimus 最早是「最富足」，后来才成「最好」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the sense: optimal performance, optimal conditions, optimal dose.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出义项：最佳性能、最适条件、最佳剂量。

normal.en: Suboptimal is the useful opposite for anything below the best.
normal.cn: suboptimal 是表示「未达最佳」的常用反义说法。

abstract.en: Optimal is a ruler that stops exactly at the mark, with no spare space.
abstract.cn: 最优是一把正好停在刻度上的尺子，不留多余空隙。

abstract.en: There can be only one top of a scale, which is why the word tolerates no better.
abstract.cn: 一个刻度只能有一个顶点，所以这个词容不下「更好」。

abstract.en: In engineering the peak is a compromise, not a triumph.
abstract.cn: 在工程里，顶点是折中，而不是凯旋。

examples.en: The optimal route avoids both the tunnel and the rush hour.
examples.cn: 最优路线既避开隧道，也避开高峰时段。

examples.en: An optimal diet is not the same for every patient.
examples.cn: 最佳饮食对每位病人并不相同。

examples.en: The engine runs at optimal speed only in cool air.
examples.cn: 这台发动机只在凉爽空气中才以最佳转速运行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「欧普提莫」——挑到最顶上那一个：最佳的

root: 拉丁 optimus「最好的」，是 bonus「好的」的补充式最高级；更深来源一般认为与 ops「资源、力量」相关，亦有「最高处」的解释，词根来源不确定。中性 optimum 先作名词「最佳值」，英语十九世纪再加 -al 构成形容词，确切首见年代不确定；suboptimal 由 sub- 加 optimal 构成。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the best result through conditions, mathematics, economics, medicine, engineering and biology to the ordinary reasoned choice.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从最好的结果出发，经条件、数学、经济、医学、工程与生物学，最后落到日常有理由的选择。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler that stops exactly at the mark, no spare space either side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把正好停在刻度上的尺子，两边都不留余地。

branches.en: THE BEST RESULT: the highest outcome the limits allow.
branches.cn: 最好的结果：条件允许范围内的最高结果。

branches.en: THE TUNED CONDITIONS AND THE WISE CHOICE: the setting that suits a process and the choice a person judges best.
branches.cn: 调好的条件与明智的选择：适合某过程的环境，以及人判断为最好的选择。

branches.en: THE MATHEMATICAL POINT: where a function reaches its best value.
branches.cn: 数学上的点：函数取得最优值之处。

branches.en: THE BALANCED ALLOCATION: resources used without waste and a design trade-off settled.
branches.cn: 平衡的配置：资源无浪费地使用，设计权衡得以定案。

branches.en: THE BEST FIT FOR A BODY: the dose that helps most and the habit that suits an environment.
branches.cn: 对身体的最佳适配：收益最大的剂量与最适应环境的习性。

intro.en: Optimal is the Latin best-stem optimus plus the English suffix -al; its noun optimum and its opposite suboptimal came later.
intro.cn: optimal 是拉丁语「最好」词干 optimus 加英语后缀 -al；名词 optimum 与反义形式 suboptimal 都后起。

latinIntro.en: Optimus supplies the superlative, ops is the disputed deeper connection, and optimum supplies the noun.
latinIntro.cn: optimus 提供最高级，ops 是有争议的更深关联，optimum 提供名词。

items.example: The superlative closes the scale at the top.
items.exampleCN: 最高级把刻度封在顶端。

items.example: Bonus supplies the positive that optimus replaces.
items.exampleCN: bonus 提供由 optimus 顶替的原级。

items.example: The disputed connection would make best originally richest.
items.exampleCN: 有争议的关联会让「最好」最早意为「最富足」。

items.structure: Latin neuter adjective used as noun
items.example: Mathematics borrowed the neuter as a noun.
items.exampleCN: 数学把这个中性形式借作名词。

items.example: English adds -al to the Latin stem.
The adverb marks the manner of reaching the peak.
items.exampleCN: 副词标出达到顶点的方式。

items.example: The noun belongs to mathematics and economics.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词属于数学与经济学。

items.meaning: to make as good as possible
items.example: The verb is built on optimum, not on optimal.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词由 optimum 构成，不是由 optimal。

items.example: The prefix names a level below the best.
items.exampleCN: 前缀命名低于最佳的水平。

items.example: It also builds final, formal and general.
items.exampleCN: 它也构成 final、formal 与 general。

definition_zh: 寡头垄断的；寡头市场的
definition_en: relating to a market dominated by a few sellers
core_image: 棋盘上只留下四枚同色棋子，其余格子空着，四枚棋子互相牵制
scene: 棋盘上只剩四枚同色棋子，彼此隔着几格，谁也不肯先动。 The airline industry remains oligopolistic despite repeated attempts at liberalization.
sceneCN: 这里 oligopolistic 指「由少数卖方主导的」（第 1 个义项：具有寡头市场结构特征的）；句意为尽管多次推动自由化，航空业仍呈寡头格局。图中可辨识物件：四枚同色棋子、空棋盘格、相互牵制的距离、未动的棋子。

pos.zh: 寡头垄断的；寡头市场的

senses.title: Having the shape of few-seller market
senses.titleCN: 呈少数卖方市场形态的
senses.definition: describing a market whose supply is concentrated in a small number of firms
senses.definitionCN: 描述供给集中在少数几家企业的市场
senses.example: The telecom sector has an oligopolistic shape.
senses.exampleCN: 电信行业呈寡头形态。
senses.why: oligopoly plus -istic gives the adjective of resemblance, parallel to monopolistic.
senses.whyCN: oligopoly 加 -istic 构成表示相似的形容词，与 monopolistic 平行。

senses.title: Pricing by a few sellers
senses.definition: describing prices set by a small group that watches one another
senses.definitionCN: 描述由相互观望的小群体设定的价格
senses.example: Oligopolistic pricing kept fares almost equal across the three airlines.
senses.exampleCN: 寡头定价使三家航空公司的票价几乎相同。
senses.why: the adjective attaches to the price behaviour that the structure produces.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词附着于该结构所产生的价格行为。

senses.title: Rivalry among the few
senses.definition: describing competition in which each move is answered by the others
senses.definitionCN: 描述一种每一步都被其余几家回应的竞争
senses.example: Oligopolistic competition runs through advertising rather than price.
senses.exampleCN: 寡头竞争通过广告而非价格展开。
senses.why: with few players, every action is visible, so rivalry becomes a sequence of responses.
senses.whyCN: 参与者少，每个动作都可见，竞争便成为一连串回应。

senses.title: Given to tacit collusion
senses.definition: describing a market where the few can align without a formal agreement
senses.definitionCN: 描述少数几家无需正式协议就能取得一致的市场
senses.example: The regulator found oligopolistic coordination in fuel surcharges.
senses.exampleCN: 监管者发现燃油附加费存在寡头式协同。
senses.why: the adjective can describe behaviour as well as structure, and collusion is the behaviour most feared.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词既可描述结构也可描述行为，而合谋是最受担忧的行为。

senses.title: Belonging to a highly concentrated industry
senses.definition: describing an industry where the top few hold most of the market
senses.definitionCN: 描述前几家占有大部分市场的产业
senses.example: The rating agencies form an oligopolistic industry of three firms.
senses.exampleCN: 评级机构构成由三家企业组成的寡头产业。
senses.why: concentration ratios give the adjective a measurable threshold in industrial economics.
senses.whyCN: 集中度比率在产业经济学中给这个形容词一个可测量的门槛。

senses.title: Behind high entry barriers
senses.titleCN: 处于高进入壁垒之后的
senses.definition: describing a market where the few are protected by costs or rules that block newcomers
senses.definitionCN: 描述少数几家受成本或规则保护、新来者难以进入的市场
senses.example: An oligopolistic market can persist because new refineries are too expensive.
senses.exampleCN: 寡头市场能够持续，因为新建炼厂过于昂贵。
senses.why: the few survive only while entry stays hard, so the adjective often implies a barrier.
senses.whyCN: 只有当进入仍然困难时少数几家才能存活，因此这个形容词常含壁垒之意。

senses.title: As regulators describe a sector
senses.titleCN: 监管者描述某一行业时的用语
senses.definition: the label competition authorities use for a sector they consider too concentrated
senses.definitionCN: 竞争主管机构用来指称其认为过于集中的行业的标签
senses.example: The report called the funeral market oligopolistic and recommended review.
senses.exampleCN: 报告称殡葬市场为寡头市场，并建议审查。
senses.why: legal usage prefers the adjective because it describes a condition without alleging a specific violation.
senses.whyCN: 法律用法偏好这个形容词，因为它描述一种状态，而不指控具体违法行为。

senses.title: Held by a few in any field
senses.titleCN: 任何领域由少数把持的
senses.definition: describing any domain where a handful of actors control access
senses.definitionCN: 描述任何由少数行为者控制准入的领域
senses.example: The awards circuit remains oligopolistic, with four studios taking most nominations.
senses.exampleCN: 评奖圈仍呈寡头格局，四家制片厂拿走大部分提名。
senses.why: the adjective leaves economics once access anywhere is controlled by a small group.
senses.whyCN: 一旦任何领域的准入被小群体控制，这个形容词就走出经济学。

intro.en: Oligopolistic is an English derivative of oligopoly, formed with the suffix complex -ist plus -ic, the same pattern as monopolistic. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: oligopolistic 是 oligopoly 的英语派生词，由 -ist 加 -ic 的后缀组合构成，与 monopolistic 同一模式。年代均为约数。

items.en: Oligos 'few' supplies the first element, the same root that opens oligarchy.
items.cn: oligos「少数」提供第一成分，与 oligarchy 开头同一词根。

items.en: Pōlein 'to sell' supplies the second element, unchanged from monopoly and duopoly.
items.cn: pōlein「卖」提供第二成分，与 monopoly、duopoly 中相同。

items.en: The noun was coined in late nineteenth-century economics on the model of monopoly.
items.cn: 这个名词于 19 世纪后期仿 monopoly 在经济学中造出。

items.en: English added -ist for a participant and -ic for the relating adjective, so oligopolist came before oligopolistic.
items.cn: 英语先加 -ist 表示参与者，再加 -ic 构成关系形容词，因此 oligopolist 先于 oligopolistic。

items.en: The adjective appears in twentieth-century industrial economics, once concentration ratios made few-seller markets measurable.
items.cn: 这个形容词出现在 20 世纪产业经济学中，当时集中度比率使少数卖方市场变得可测量。

items.en: The exact first printed use is not recorded. The suffix chain is fully documented and the Greek elements are attested.
items.cn: 最早印刷用例没有确切记录。后缀链条有完整书证，希腊成分也有据可查。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same compound and one same-root look-alike; group two holds adjectives that describe concentration or exclusion without naming the structure.
note.cn: 第一组是同出该复合词的词形，以及一个同根形近词；第二组是描述集中或排除、却不指称该结构的形容词。

entries.definition: The structure itself; oligopolistic is the adjective that describes it.
entries.definitionCN: 结构本身；oligopolistic 是描述它的形容词。

entries.definition: The parallel adjective for a single dominant seller; the suffix is the same, the first element is not.
entries.definitionCN: 平行形容词，用于单一支配卖方；后缀相同，第一成分不同。

entries.definition: From oligos plus archein 'to rule', meaning governed by a small group; its second element is political, not commercial.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 oligos 加 archein「统治」，意为由小群体治理；第二成分是政治的，而非商业的。

entries.definition: The adjective for exactly two sellers, the narrowest case of an oligopolistic market.
entries.definitionCN: 恰好两家卖方的形容词，是寡头市场中最窄的情形。

entries.definition: Describing a market where a large share sits with few firms; concentration is a measure, not a structure.
entries.definitionCN: 描述很大份额集中于少数企业的市场；集中度是一种度量，而非结构。

entries.definition: Describing an industry organized through agreements; an oligopolistic market may be cartelized, but not all are.
entries.definitionCN: 描述通过协议组织起来的产业；寡头市场可能被卡特尔化，但并非全都如此。

entries.definition: Describing terms that do not reflect rivalry; it names the result, while oligopolistic names the structure.
entries.definitionCN: 描述不反映竞争的条款；它指结果，而 oligopolistic 指结构。

entries.definition: Describing practices that limit what others may do; restrictive conduct can occur in a market that is not oligopolistic.
entries.definitionCN: 描述限制他人可为之事的行为；限制性行为也可发生在非寡头市场。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: oligopoly + -ist + -ic: the adjective of the few-seller structure.
normal.cn: oligopoly + -ist + -ic：少数卖方结构的形容词。

normal.en: The family runs oligopoly, oligopolist, oligopolistically, duopoly, monopoly.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 oligopoly、oligopolist、oligopolistically、duopoly、monopoly。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the market sense: oligopolistic market, oligopolistic pricing, oligopolistic competition.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出市场义：寡头市场、寡头定价、寡头竞争。

normal.en: Its parallel is monopolistic: same suffix, first element changed from one to few.
normal.cn: 它的平行词是 monopolistic：后缀相同，第一成分从「一」变为「少数」。

normal.en: The look-alike oligarchic uses the root for rule, not the root for selling.
normal.cn: 形近词 oligarchic 用的是「统治」词根，而非「卖」词根。

abstract.en: Picture four pieces on a board with every other square empty.
abstract.cn: 想象棋盘上只剩四枚棋子，其余格子全空。

abstract.en: Picture four doors on one corridor and no other corridor to enter.
abstract.cn: 想象一条走廊上只有四扇门，没有别的走廊可进。

abstract.en: Picture four prices written on one board in the same handwriting.
abstract.cn: 想象四家价格写在同一块牌上，笔迹都一样。

examples.en: The market for operating systems is oligopolistic rather than open.
examples.cn: 操作系统市场呈寡头格局，而非开放市场。

examples.en: Oligopolistic pricing can keep margins high even when demand falls.
examples.cn: 即使需求下降，寡头定价也能维持较高利润率。

examples.en: Regulators described the fuel retail sector as highly oligopolistic.
examples.cn: 监管者称燃油零售业高度寡头化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「oligopoly（寡头）+ istic（……的）」——少数几家说了算的 → 寡头垄断的

root: oligopoly（希腊 oligos「少数」+ pōlein「卖」，仿 monopoly 于 19 世纪后期造出）+ 后缀 -ist + -ic，构成「寡头市场特征的」形容词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one small group: a market takes the shape of few sellers, and that shape is then read as structure, pricing, rivalry, coordination, concentration, barriers, regulatory label, and finally any field held by a few.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个小群体展开：市场呈现出少数卖方的形状，这个形状再被读作结构、定价、竞争、协同、集中度、壁垒、监管标签，最后是任何由少数把持的领域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: four pieces left on a board, each watching the others.
core.cn: 核心意象：棋盘上只剩四枚棋子，彼此盯着对方。

branches.en: SHAPE AND PRICE: the few-seller form, and the prices it produces.
branches.cn: 形态与价格：少数卖方的形态，以及它所产生的价格。

branches.en: RIVALRY AND COORDINATION: moves answered move by move, and the quiet alignment that can follow.
branches.cn: 竞争与协同：一步被一步回应，以及随后可能出现的安静一致。

branches.en: CONCENTRATION: the top few hold most of the market.
branches.cn: 集中度：前几家握住大部分市场。

branches.en: BARRIERS AND LABEL: newcomers blocked by cost, and the word regulators put on the sector.
branches.cn: 壁垒与标签：新来者被成本挡住，以及监管者贴在该行业上的词。

branches.en: ANY SMALL CIRCLE: four studios, four clubs, any field held by a handful.
branches.cn: 任何小圈子：四家制片厂、四家俱乐部，任何被少数把持的领域。

intro.en: The adjective piles an English suffix complex onto a Greek-style compound, so the compound and the ending can be read separately.
intro.cn: 这个形容词在一个希腊式复合词上叠了英语后缀组合，因此复合词与词尾可以分开读。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base word here; the pattern of -isticus came through French from Greek -istikos, while oligos and pōlein remain Greek.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁基础词；-isticus 的模式经法语来自希腊 -istikos，而 oligos 与 pōlein 仍是希腊语。

items.example: The element also appears in oligarchy.
items.exampleCN: 这个成分也出现在 oligarchy 中。

items.example: The selling element stays unchanged across the family.
items.exampleCN: 「卖」这个成分在整个词族中保持不变。

items.example: Each oligopolist matched the rival's cut.
items.exampleCN: 每个寡头都跟随对手降价。
这三家企业以寡头方式定价。

items.example: The duopolistic route raised fares together.
items.exampleCN: 这条双寡头航线一起提价。

items.example: The club had an oligarchic board.
items.exampleCN: 俱乐部有一个寡头式董事会。

definition_zh: 缓和；减轻；平息；满足
definition_en: to make an unpleasant feeling less intense, or to satisfy a desire
core_image: 一只手轻按波涛，水面渐渐归于平静
scene: 暴雨过后洪水未退，堤上一夜未眠的人们终于听到水声低了下去。 Officials worked through the night to assuage the flood fears of the town.
sceneCN: 这里 assuage 是「缓和、平息」（第 1 个义项：减轻强烈的情绪）；句意为官员们连夜工作以平息镇民对洪水的恐惧。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「缓和；减轻」
同根形容词，义为「温和的；圆滑的」

senses.title: To ease a painful feeling
senses.definition: to make grief, fear, or pain less intense
senses.definitionCN: 使悲伤、恐惧或痛苦变得不那么强烈
senses.example: A warm meal can assuage sorrow for a while.
senses.exampleCN: 一顿热饭能暂时抚慰悲伤。
senses.why: Latin suavis meant sweet; sweetening a harsh feeling softens it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 suavis 意为甜；给苦涩的情绪加点甜，它就缓和了。

senses.title: To satisfy a desire
senses.definition: to fulfil a craving such as hunger or curiosity
senses.definitionCN: 满足如饥饿、好奇之类的渴求
senses.example: Nothing could assuage his hunger for news.
senses.exampleCN: 什么都满足不了他对消息的渴求。
senses.why: A craving is an inner turbulence; satisfying it calms the surge.
senses.whyCN: 渴求是内心的翻腾；满足它便平息了这股涌动。

intro.en: Assuage comes from Old French asuagier, from Vulgar Latin *assuaviare, to sweeten, from Latin suavis.
intro.cn: assuage 源自古法语 asuagier，出自通俗拉丁语 *assuaviare（使变甜），词根为拉丁语 suavis（甜的）。

items.en: The root *swād- meant sweet.
items.cn: 词根 *swād- 意为甜。

items.en: Suavis meant sweet, pleasant.
items.cn: 拉丁语 suavis 意为甜的、令人愉快的。

items.en: Assuaviare meant to make sweet, hence to soften.
items.cn: 通俗拉丁语 assuaviare 意为使变甜，进而引申为使缓和。

items.en: Asuagier meant to calm or appease.
items.cn: 古法语 asuagier 意为使平静、安抚。

items.en: English adopted assuage in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语借入 assuage。

note.en: Assuage sweetens turmoil: the same root gives suave its smooth charm.
note.cn: assuage 给纷扰加糖：同根的 suave 也带着温和顺滑。

entries.definition: smoothly agreeable in manner
entries.definitionCN: 温文尔雅的（同根形容词）

entries.definition: the act of persuading
entries.definitionCN: 说服（同根名词）

entries.definition: to win over by talking
entries.definitionCN: 说服（同根）

entries.definition: similar opening letters, opposite meaning, different root
entries.definitionCN: 袭击（开头形似，意义相反，词源不同）

entries.definition: English cousin of the sweet root
entries.definitionCN: 甜的（同词根的英语表亲）

entries.definition: to soften someone's anger
entries.definitionCN: 抚慰；使息怒

entries.definition: to pacify by giving in
entries.definitionCN: 安抚；绥靖

entries.definition: to make less severe
entries.definitionCN: 减轻；缓解

entries.definition: to lay to rest a fear or doubt
entries.definitionCN: 平息；消除

entries.definition: to calm by pleasing
entries.definitionCN: 安抚

normalIntro.en: As + suage: think a-swaging, like a wave being smoothed flat.
normalIntro.cn: 把 assuage 想成 a-swage：像把一块铁敲平，把情绪熨平。

normal.en: suavis means sweet, the root of the word.
normal.cn: 词根 suavis 意为甜。

normal.en: sweeten a feeling to soften it.
normal.cn: 给情绪加甜即是软化。

normal.en: suave shares the same sweet root.
normal.cn: suave 同出甜的词根。

normal.en: common objects are fears and guilt.
normal.cn: 常见宾语是恐惧与内疚。

normal.en: it can also mean satisfy a craving.
normal.cn: 它也可表示满足渴求。

abstract.en: Picture honey stirred into bitter tea.
abstract.cn: 想象蜂蜜搅进苦茶。

abstract.en: See a storm easing into a drizzle.
abstract.cn: 看见暴风雨缓和成细雨。

abstract.en: Feel a clenched fist slowly opening.
abstract.cn: 体会紧握的拳头缓缓松开。

examples.en: The envoy's words assuaged the crowd's anger.
examples.cn: 特使的话平息了人群的怒火。

examples.en: He ate quickly to assuage his hunger.
examples.cn: 他狼吞虎咽以解饥饿。

examples.en: Nothing could assuage her grief that winter.
examples.cn: 那年冬天什么都抚不平她的悲伤。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额斯为奇」——额视此物为奇甜之药，苦痛得解即 assuage。

root: 拉丁语 suavis（甜的）→ 通俗拉丁语 *assuaviare（使变甜）→ 古法语 asuagier（安抚）→ 英语 assuage（缓和；平息）。

sensesIntro.en: Sweetening a turmoil eases both raw feelings and inner cravings.
sensesIntro.cn: 给纷扰加甜，既抚平情绪，也喂饱欲求。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: honey poured onto a storm
core.cn: 核心意象：往风暴上浇蜂蜜

branches.en: easing grief or fear
branches.cn: 抚平悲伤或恐惧

branches.en: feeding a craving
branches.cn: 满足渴求

branches.en: the sweet root at work
branches.cn: 甜的词根在起作用

branches.en: gentle pacifying of anger
branches.cn: 温和地平息怒气

branches.en: quieting an inner surge
branches.cn: 平息内心的涌动

intro.en: The sweet root links soothing with pleasing, from taste to temper.
intro.cn: 甜的词根把抚慰与愉悦相连，从味觉到心绪。

latinIntro.en: Latin suavis, sweet, anchors the assuage family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 suavis（甜）是 assuage 词族的锚点。

definition_zh: 先于；在……之前；走在前面；位次高于；作为……的前身
definition_en: to come or go before something or someone in time, order, position, or rank
core_image: 一个人先一步走过路口，后面的人还没到
scene: 颁奖典礼之前先有一段简短的致辞。 A short speech preceded the award ceremony.
sceneCN: 这里 precede 是「在时间上先于」（第 1 个义项）；句意：颁奖典礼之前先有一段简短致辞。场景要点：先后顺序、前一件先发生、后一件才登场；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 先于；在……之前；走在前面；位次高于

senses.title: To happen earlier in time
senses.titleCN: 先于：在时间上更早发生
senses.definition: to happen or exist before something else in time
senses.definitionCN: 在时间上比另一事物更早发生或存在
senses.example: A short speech preceded the award ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 颁奖典礼之前先有一段简短致辞。
senses.why: Latin praecedere is prae 'before' plus cedere 'go'. The first sense is simply going earlier along the timeline.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 praecedere 是 prae“在前”加 cedere“走”。第一个义项就是沿着时间线走得更早。

senses.title: To come earlier in an order
senses.definition: to come before something else in a sequence, list, or arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 在序列、清单或排列中位于另一事物之前
senses.example: The prefix precedes the root in this word.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个词里，前缀排在词根之前。
senses.why: Time becomes sequence. What goes first on a line is what has preceded the rest, even when no clock is involved.
senses.whyCN: 时间变成了顺序。在一条线上排在最前的，就是先于其余各项的，即使不涉及钟表。

senses.title: To walk in front of
senses.definition: to go in front of someone, especially in a procession or on a route
senses.definitionCN: 走在某人前面，尤指在游行队伍或行进路线上
senses.example: A drummer preceded the bridal party down the street.
senses.exampleCN: 一名鼓手走在迎亲队伍前面，沿街而行。
senses.why: This is the literal picture of the Latin verb: one body moving ahead of another along the same road.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁动词最字面的画面：一具身体沿着同一条路走在另一具前面。

senses.title: To outrank or take priority
senses.titleCN: 优先：位次或重要性在前
senses.definition: to be higher in rank, importance, or priority than someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 在级别、重要性或优先次序上高于某人或某物
senses.example: In this court, federal law precedes state law.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个法庭上，联邦法优先于州法。
senses.why: A procession has an order of dignity as well as an order in space. Whoever goes first is served first, so position becomes priority.
senses.whyCN: 队伍不只有空间顺序，还有尊卑顺序。走在前面的人先被招待，于是位置变成了优先权。

senses.title: To go ahead as an introduction
senses.titleCN: 先行开道：把后面的引出来
senses.definition: to come before something as its introduction or preparation
senses.definitionCN: 作为某事物的引子或准备而出现在它之前
senses.example: A period of quiet preceded the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨之前有一段平静。
senses.why: What goes first can prepare the way for what follows. The earlier thing is not merely earlier; it ushers the later one in.
senses.whyCN: 走在前面的东西可以为后面的东西铺路。先前之物不只是更早，它还把后来者引了进来。

senses.title: To be the forerunner of
senses.definition: to be an earlier form or ancestor of something that came later
senses.definitionCN: 是后来某事物的较早形态或前身
senses.example: The telegraph preceded the telephone by decades.
senses.exampleCN: 电报比电话早出现了几十年。
senses.why: Objects too can walk in a line through history. The older device stands in front of the newer one, which is its descendant.
senses.whyCN: 物件也能在历史中排队行走。较老的装置站在较新的前面，后者是它的后裔。

senses.title: To preface with words
senses.titleCN: 开场先说：用话在前面铺一层
senses.definition: to say something before the main statement or text
senses.definitionCN: 在主要陈述或正文之前先说一些话
senses.example: He preceded his refusal with a long apology.
senses.exampleCN: 他在拒绝之前先说了很长一段道歉。
senses.why: Speech has an order too. Words placed in front of the main message are doing the walking-ahead.
senses.whyCN: 言语也有顺序。放在主要信息前面的那些话，承担的就是“走在前面”的功能。

senses.title: Literary: to have gone before others
senses.titleCN: 书面：先走一步（指已故的先辈）
senses.definition: in formal or literary use, to have gone before others, especially to have died earlier
senses.definitionCN: 在正式或文学用法中，指先于他人离去，尤指更早去世
senses.example: We honor those who preceded us and built this town.
senses.exampleCN: 我们敬重那些先我们而去、建起这座小镇的人。
senses.why: A procession through life has a front and a back. Those already further along are described as having preceded the living.
senses.whyCN: 穿越一生的队伍有前有后。已经走得更远的人，就被说成先于在世者而行。

intro.en: Precede is a transparent Latin compound: before plus go. Nearly all of its English senses are versions of that one physical picture.
intro.cn: precede 是一个构造透明的拉丁复合词：“在前”加“走”。它在英语里的几乎每个义项，都是这一幅身体画面的变体。

items.en: Prae meant 'before, in front of'. It is the source of the English prefix pre-, and it marks position in space as well as priority in time.
items.cn: prae 意为“在前、在……之前”。它是英语前缀 pre- 的来源，既标记空间位置，也标记时间上的优先。

items.en: Cedere meant 'to go, to yield, to withdraw'. English gets cede, accede, exceed, proceed, and succeed from this verb.
items.cn: cedere 意为“走、让、退”。英语的 cede、accede、exceed、proceed、succeed 都出自这个动词。

items.en: Praecedere meant 'to go before, to precede'. It described both people walking ahead and events coming earlier.
items.cn: praecedere 意为“走在前面、先于”。它既描述人走在前头，也描述事件更早发生。

items.en: Old French took the verb as preceder, keeping the sense of going or coming before.
items.cn: 古法语把这个动词接作 preceder，保留“走在前面、先来”的意思。

items.en: English precede is recorded in the 15th century. The legal noun precedent and the noun precedence grow from the same root.
items.cn: 英语 precede 记录于 15 世纪。法律名词 precedent 与名词 precedence 都从同一个词根长出。

items.en: Modern usage extends the image to ranks, arguments, inventions, and even the dead: whatever stands earlier in a line has preceded what stands later.
items.cn: 现代用法把这幅画面扩展到等级、论证、发明，甚至逝者：凡在一条线上站得更早的，就先于站得更晚的。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb for going. The second group collects words for coming before in time, order, and rank.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语表示“走”的动词。第二组收表示“在时间、顺序、等级上在前”的词。

entries.definition: to go forward or continue. Pro- 'forward' plus cedere 'go', so it moves ahead rather than before.
entries.definitionCN: 前进或继续进行。pro-“向前”加 cedere“走”，所以它是向前走，而非走在前面。

entries.definition: an earlier case used as a rule for later ones. It is the noun of precede in legal usage.
entries.definitionCN: 被用作后来案例规则的先前判例。它是 precede 在法律用法中的名词。

entries.definition: the person who held a post before another. From Latin prae- plus decedere 'to go away', literally one who went before.
entries.definitionCN: 在某人之前担任某职位的人。来自拉丁 prae- 加 decedere“离开”，字面即“先走的人”。

entries.definition: the right to go or be treated first. It is the abstract noun of precede.
entries.definitionCN: 先行或被优先对待的权利。它是 precede 的抽象名词。

entries.definition: to exist or happen before something in date. Predate is narrower, used only of time.
entries.definitionCN: 在日期上早于某事物。predate 更窄，只用于时间。

entries.definition: to be earlier than, or to put an earlier date on. Antedate is formal and often about documents.
entries.definitionCN: 早于，或在文件上写较早的日期。antedate 较正式，常用于文件。

entries.definition: to go in front and show the way. Lead implies guiding; precede only states the order.
entries.definitionCN: 走在前面并带路。lead 含引导之意；precede 只陈述先后顺序。

entries.definition: to have a higher rank than someone. Outrank matches sense 04 exactly and is used of people and offices.
entries.definitionCN: 级别高于某人。outrank 精确对应第 4 义项，多用于人与职位。

entries.definition: to go before as a sign or precursor. Forerun is literary and rare; its noun forerunner is common.
entries.definitionCN: 作为征兆或先驱先行。forerun 带文学色彩且少见；其名词 forerunner 更常用。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks: the walker ahead, the prefix before the root, the court that hears federal law first, the older machine, and the ancestors.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手：走在前面的人、词根前的前缀、先审联邦法的法庭、更老的机器、先辈。

normal.en: Pre- means before, cede means go. Precede is literally before-go.
normal.cn: pre- 是“在前”，cede 是“走”。precede 字面就是“先走”。

normal.en: In the word unhappy, un- precedes happy: it walks in front of the root.
normal.cn: 在 unhappy 这个词里，un- 走在 happy 前面，就是 precede 词根。

normal.en: Take precedence: whoever walks first gets served first.
normal.cn: take precedence：谁走在前面，谁先被招待。

normal.en: The telegraph preceded the telephone; the older machine stands in front of the newer one in history's queue.
normal.cn: 电报先于电话；在历史的队伍里，更老的机器站在更新的前面。

normal.en: Those who preceded us are the ones already further up the road.
normal.cn: 先我们而去的人，就是已经在路上走得更远的那些。

abstract.en: Order is not a thing in the world but a line we draw; precede is the word for standing on the earlier side of that line.
abstract.cn: 顺序不是世界里的物件，而是我们画的线；precede 就是在一条线较早一侧站着的说法。

abstract.en: Priority borrows its grammar from walking: we say law comes first as if laws had legs.
abstract.cn: 优先权借用了行走的语法：我们说法律“在先”，仿佛法律长了腿。

abstract.en: Every forerunner is only recognized as one after the thing it preceded has arrived.
abstract.cn: 每一个前身，都只有在它所先行的那件事到来之后，才被认出来是前身。

examples.en: The years preceding the war were marked by rapid industrial growth.
examples.cn: 战前那些年以快速的工业增长为标志。

examples.en: In the protocol, the chair's remarks precede the vote.
examples.cn: 按议程，主席发言在投票之前。

examples.en: Several small tremors preceded the main earthquake.
examples.cn: 主震之前发生了数次小震动。

dict_mnemonic.text: “普瑞西德”——普瑞先一步西德而行，就是 precede（先于、走在前面）

root: 拉丁语 praecedere＝prae“在前”+ cedere“走” → 古法语 preceder → 英语 precede（15 世纪）；与 proceed、precedent、predecessor、cede 同根。

sensesIntro.en: One physical image serves everything: something moves ahead of something else on the same line. Time, sequence, space, rank, introduction, ancestry, and even death are all lines along which one item can stand before another.
sensesIntro.cn: 一幅身体画面统摄全部义项：某物在同一条线上走在另一物前面。时间、顺序、空间、等级、引子、前身，甚至死亡，都是可以让一个项目站在另一个之前的线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one walker a few steps ahead of another on the same road.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一条路上，一个行者比另一个领先几步。

branches.en: TIME AND SEQUENCE: earlier on the timeline or in the list.
branches.cn: 时间与顺序：在时间线上或清单里更早。

branches.en: SPACE: a body moving in front along a route.
branches.cn: 空间：一具身体沿路线走在前面。

branches.en: RANK: position turned into priority and precedence.
branches.cn: 等级：位置变成优先权与位次。

branches.en: INTRODUCTION: what goes first to prepare or frame what follows.
branches.cn: 引子：先走一步，为后面的东西铺路或定框。

branches.en: LINEAGE: the earlier device and the people already further along.
branches.cn: 谱系：更早的器物，以及已经走得更远的人。

intro.en: Precede is built from a prefix of position and a verb of motion. The same two pieces, with other prefixes, produce much of the vocabulary of going and yielding.
intro.cn: precede 由一个表位置的前缀和一个表运动的动词构成。同样两个构件配上别的前缀，产出了大量表示“行走与让渡”的词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin praecedere passed into French and English; its participle and noun forms supplied precedent, precedence, and predecessor.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 praecedere 传入法语与英语；它的分词与名词形式提供了 precedent、precedence、predecessor。

items.meaningCN: 表示施动者或性质的后缀
表示状态或性质的名词后缀

definition_zh: 定价；定价工作；价格体系
definition_en: the activity or system of setting prices for goods and services
core_image: 一张价目表被反复改写，铅笔字迹一层盖着一层，旁边的成本单也在变
scene: 商店后仓里，经理在价目表上来回改动，成本单摊在手边，铅笔痕迹叠了好几层。 Transparent pricing reduced complaints at the counter.
sceneCN: 这里 pricing 指「为商品设定价格的做法与体系」（第 1 个义项：定价这一活动本身）；句意为透明的定价减少了柜台前的投诉。图中可辨识物件：反复改写的价目表、成本单、铅笔、后仓货架。

pos.zh: 定价；定价工作（不可数）；也可作定语，如定价策略、定价模式

senses.title: The work of setting prices
senses.definition: the ongoing activity of deciding what to charge for goods or services
senses.definitionCN: 决定商品或服务收多少钱的持续活动
senses.example: Pricing takes more time than the sales staff expect.
senses.exampleCN: 定价所花的时间比销售人员预想的多。
senses.why: the -ing form names the activity itself, not any single price that results from it.
senses.whyCN: -ing 形式指活动本身，而非由此产生的某一个价格。

senses.title: A firm's price system
senses.definition: the schedule of charges a seller applies across its products
senses.definitionCN: 卖方在其全部商品上采用的价格表
senses.example: Its pricing is simple: one rate for every size.
senses.exampleCN: 它的价格体系很简单：所有规格一个价。
senses.why: pricing can stand for the whole schedule because what is set is a system, not one number.
senses.whyCN: pricing 可以指整张价格表，因为被设定的是体系，而非单一数字。

senses.title: A pricing decision
senses.definition: a specific choice about what to charge, often made at a meeting
senses.definitionCN: 关于收多少钱的具体选择，常在会议上作出
senses.example: The pricing decision was postponed until the cost report arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 定价决策被推迟到成本报告送达之后。
senses.why: business writing uses the gerund attributively for discrete decisions within the activity.
senses.whyCN: 商业写作把这个动名词作定语，指该活动中的一项项具体决策。

senses.title: A method of arriving at a price
senses.definition: the procedure used to calculate a price, such as cost-plus or value-based
senses.definitionCN: 计算价格所用的程序，如成本加成或价值导向
senses.example: Cost-based pricing ignores what buyers are willing to pay.
senses.exampleCN: 成本导向定价忽略买主愿意付多少。
senses.why: the word shifts from the act to the method once analysts compare approaches.
senses.whyCN: 当分析者比较不同做法时，这个词就从动作转向方法。

senses.title: The level at which prices sit
senses.definition: the general height of charges relative to cost or to rivals
senses.definitionCN: 收费相对于成本或对手的总体高度
senses.example: Premium pricing kept the brand's margins high for years.
senses.exampleCN: 溢价定价让这个品牌的利润率多年保持高位。
senses.why: the gerund can name a level as well as an act when the question is how high prices are.
senses.whyCN: 当问题落在价格有多高时，这个动名词也可以指水平，而不只是动作。

senses.title: Dynamic and algorithmic pricing
senses.definition: setting prices by rules or software that change with demand and stock
senses.definitionCN: 由随需求与库存变动的规则或软件来设定价格
